In this paper, we present a field-sensitive taint analysis that combines Data Structure Analysis (DSA) for field-sensitive points-to information with a data-flow analysis for tracking explicit dependencies. We identify that existing DSA-style analyses lose precision on a common object pattern: a C struct object that mixes scalar fields with a flexible array member. When such an array is accessed with symbolic indices, DSA loses points-to field sensitivity for the entire object, inflating false alarms in the data-flow analysis. To address this, we propose I-DSA, which extends DSA by representing field positions as intervals, so that a pointer with symbolic bounds merges only the fields within those bounds. We further develop a sound data-flow analysis based on abstract interpretation. We implement I-DSA on top of SeaDSA and the data-flow analysis inside Crab. Our tool targets LLVM IR and supports configurable taint policies by instrumenting the IR with taint intrinsics. Our experiments show that I-DSA reduces the false alarms caused by this pattern at little cost in the pointer analysis, that SVF, an inclusion-based pointer analysis, shows a similar field-sensitivity loss, and that our tai

3ebb5c022acd2d35e43096bc.title_original: K-out-of-N Oblivious Transfer over Erasure Channels: Capacity and Reductions
3ebb5c022acd2d35e43096bc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21359v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study $K$-out-of-$N$ oblivious transfer (OT) between a server and a client over a discrete memoryless channel, under an honest-but-curious model. The client must retrieve $K$ out of $N$ messages stored by the server while learning nothing about the remaining $N-K$ messages, and the server must not learn the client's selection. For a binary erasure channel (BEC) with parameter $\epsilon$, we show that the $K$-out-of-$N$ OT capacity is $\min\Big(\frac{K\epsilon}{N-K},1-\epsilon\Big)$. This characterization generalizes the known capacity results for $1$-out-of-$2$ OT and for $1$-out-of-$N$ OT when $\epsilon\ge\tfrac{N-1}{N}$. We also investigate OT reductions, specifically, we show that constructing a $K$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol from repeating $K$ times an optimal $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be suboptimal, but we also identify certain ranges of $\epsilon$ and $M < N$ for which a $1$-out-of-$N$ OT protocol can be optimally realized via the repetition of a $1$-out-of-$M$ OT protocol. Finally, we discuss extensions of our results to a generalized erasure channel (GEC).

63fa53277171418ea787ca97.title_original: ExclaveFL: Verifiable Claims for Federated Learning using Exclaves
63fa53277171418ea787ca97.excerpt: arXiv:2412.10537v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In federated learning (FL), data providers jointly train a machine learning model without sharing training data. This makes it challenging to provide verifiable claims about the trained model, e.g., related to the employed training data, data sanitization, or training algorithm---a malicious data provider can simply deviate from the correct training protocol without detection. Prior FL training systems have used trusted execution environments (TEEs) to protect the training computation, relying on the confidentiality and integrity of TEEs. TEE confidentiality, however, has been shown to be vulnerable to various attacks, e.g., via side channels. We describe ExclaveFL, a system for training FL models that establishes verifiable claims about models through fine-grained runtime attestation proofs. Since such proofs only require integrity, ExclaveFL generates them using exclaves, which are integrity-only execution environments without software-managed secrets, making them immune to data leakage attacks. ExclaveFL uses exclaves to attest data transformations during FL training, and the runtime attestation proofs then form an attested dataflow graph of the entire training computation. The graph is checked by an auditor to ensure that the trained model satisfies claims, e.g., about the use of data sanitization by data providers or aggregation by the model provider. Since exclaves require minor yet proprietary firmware changes, we eva

301ec6380c61746a8c8b68c5.title_original: LiteLMGuard: Seamless and Lightweight On-Device Guardrails for Small Language Models against Quantization Vulnerabilities
301ec6380c61746a8c8b68c5.excerpt: arXiv:2505.05619v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) has influenced the development of Small Language Models (SLMs) for on-device deployment across smartphones and edge devices, offering enhanced privacy, reduced latency, server-free functionality, and improved user experience. However, due to on-device resource constraints, SLMs undergo size optimization through compression techniques like quantization, which inadvertently introduce fairness, ethical and privacy risks. Critically, quantized SLMs may respond to harmful queries directly, without requiring adversarial manipulation, raising significant safety and trust concerns. To address this, we propose LiteLMGuard, an on-device guardrail that provides real-time, prompt-level defense for quantized SLMs. Additionally, our guardrail is designed to be model-agnostic such that it can be seamlessly integrated with any SLM, operating independently of underlying architectures. Our LiteLMGuard formalizes deep learning (DL)-based prompt filtering by leveraging semantic understanding to classify prompt answerability for SLMs. Built on our curated Answerable-or-Not dataset, LiteLMGuard employs ELECTRA as the candidate model with 97.75% answerability classification accuracy. The on-device deployment of LiteLMGuard enabled real-time offline filtering with over 85% defense-rate against harmful prompts (including jailbreak attacks), 94% filtering accuracy and ~135 ms average latency. These

02ae01d288b8eba538c95fff.title_original: BitBypass: A New Direction in Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models with Bitstream Camouflage
02ae01d288b8eba538c95fff.excerpt: arXiv:2506.02479v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inherent risk of generating harmful and unsafe content by Large Language Models (LLMs), has highlighted the need for their safety alignment. Various techniques like supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and red-teaming were developed for ensuring the safety alignment of LLMs. However, the robustness of these aligned LLMs is always challenged by adversarial attacks that exploit unexplored and underlying vulnerabilities of the safety alignment. In this paper, we develop a novel black-box jailbreak attack, called BitBypass, that leverages hyphen-separated bitstream camouflage for jailbreaking aligned LLMs. This represents a new direction in jailbreaking by exploiting fundamental information representation of data as continuous bits, rather than leveraging prompt engineering or adversarial manipulations. Our evaluation of five state-of-the-art LLMs, namely GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, Claude 3.5, Llama 3.1, and Mixtral, in adversarial perspective, revealed the capabilities of BitBypass in bypassing their safety alignment and tricking them into generating harmful and unsafe content. Further, we observed that BitBypass outperforms several state-of-the-art jailbreak attacks in terms of stealthiness and attack success. Overall, these results highlights the effectiveness and efficiency of BitBypass in jailbreaking these state-of-the-art LLMs.

bcbcfaa076835f2160dfb9b5.title_original: Vectorised Hashing Based on Bernstein-Rabin-Winograd Polynomials over Prime Order Fields
bcbcfaa076835f2160dfb9b5.excerpt: arXiv:2507.06490v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the new AXU hash function decBRWHash, which is parameterised by the positive integer $c$ and is based on Bernstein-Rabin-Winograd (BRW) polynomials. Choosing $c>1$ gives a hash function which can be implemented using $c$-way single instruction multiple data (SIMD) instructions. We report a set of very comprehensive hand optimised assembly implementations of 4-decBRWHash using avx2 SIMD instructions available on modern Intel processors. For comparison, we also report similar carefully optimised avx2 assembly implementations of polyHash, an AXU hash function based on usual polynomials. Our implementations are over prime order fields, specifically the primes $2^{127}-1$ and $2^{130}-5$. For the prime $2^{130}-5$, for avx2 implementations, compared to the famous Poly1305 hash function, 4-decBRWHash is faster for messages which are a few hundred bytes long and achieves a speed-up of about 16% for message lengths in a few kilobytes range and improves to a speed-up of about 23% for message lengths in a few megabytes range.

f1fe2c31cbdc6a5244eb7be2.title_original: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
f1fe2c31cbdc6a5244eb7be2.excerpt: arXiv:2510.22622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subjec

68079a3f05fa18e842ff4757.title_original: Mind the Gap: Cross-RFC Formal Analysis Exposes DNSSEC's Hidden Vulnerabilities
68079a3f05fa18e842ff4757.excerpt: arXiv:2512.11431v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a cross-RFC formal analysis of selected DNSSEC mechanisms using SAPIC+ models of cryptographic operations and stateful caching. We analyze properties concerning data origin authenticity, integrity, chain of trust, and authenticated denial of existence within these models. Our analysis shows that core authentication properties hold under the modeled assumptions, while wildcard expansion, the mechanism that bridges positive and negative authentication, exhibits a cross-RFC interaction vulnerability that defeats DNSSEC's integrity guarantee. Specifically, we discover Cross-Zone Wildcard Cache Poisoning: a new attack in which a malicious zone operator exploits a gap in the DNSSEC specifications to poison resolver caches with forged records for some domains outside its authority, served to clients as DNSSEC-authentic. The tested versions of all four major resolvers implementing the affected caching optimization accept the malformed wildcard material. The resulting impact depends on the resolver's synthesis path. All four vendors have publicly released fixes. The distinctive integrity failure is a synthesized, attacker-chosen positive answer with the Authenticated Data (AD) bit set: prior attacks instead exhausted availability, downgraded to AD=0, or skipped validation. Our models also identify two cross-RFC availability flaws and rediscover three known attack classes. We test six resolvers and measure deployme

2e8add184cd7a6ff04fc56ab.title_original: Better Call Graphs: A New Dataset of Function Call Graphs for Malware Classification
2e8add184cd7a6ff04fc56ab.excerpt: arXiv:2512.20872v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Function call graphs (FCGs) have emerged as a powerful abstraction for malware detection, capturing the behavioral structure of applications beyond surface-level signatures. Their utility in traditional program analysis has been well established, enabling effective classification and analysis of malicious software. In the mobile domain, especially in the Android ecosystem, FCG-based malware classification is particularly critical due to the platform's widespread adoption and the complex, component-based structure of Android apps. However, progress in this direction is hindered by the lack of large-scale, high-quality Android-specific FCG datasets. Existing datasets are often outdated, dominated by small or redundant graphs resulting from app repackaging, and fail to reflect the diversity of real-world malware. These limitations lead to overfitting and unreliable evaluation of graph-based classification methods. To address this gap, we introduce Better Call Graphs (BCG), a comprehensive dataset of large and unique FCGs extracted from recent Android application packages (APKs). BCG includes both benign and malicious samples spanning various families and types, along with graph-level features for each APK. Through extensive experiments using baseline classifiers, we demonstrate the necessity and value of BCG compared to existing datasets. BCG is publicly available at https://erdemub.github.io/BCG-dataset.

1bdd937594a6e58ec0ba0ab7.title_original: Clawdrain: Exploiting Tool-Calling Chains for Stealthy Token Exhaustion in OpenClaw Agents
1bdd937594a6e58ec0ba0ab7.excerpt: arXiv:2603.00902v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tool-calling LLM agents rely on third-party skills to extend their capabilities, but this openness exposes a supply-chain attack surface in which malicious skill instructions can manipulate agent execution across multiple turns. In this work, we present Clawdrain, a Trojanized OpenClaw skill that induces resource exhaustion through a Segmented Verification Process (SVP). SVP combines stateful progression, repair-driven repetition, and termination to create costly tool-calling chains while preserving a legitimate final payload. We evaluate Clawdrain in a production-like OpenClaw deployment with real API billing across Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6. Clawdrain achieves 2-16 times token amplification with plain SVP, while the three models exhibit distinct behaviors, including autoregressive compliance, proactive scripting, and extended trial-and-error reasoning. Our findings reveal that agent resource exhaustion arises not only from output generation, but also from repeated context re-ingestion, tool coordination, reasoning, and recovery, motivating system-level controls over cumulative skill behavior.

01307cd8bf95c6638b71553c.title_original: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections
01307cd8bf95c6638b71553c.excerpt: arXiv:2605.17634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Prompt injection is the most critical vulnerability in deployed AI agents. Despite recent progress, we show that the prevailing defense paradigm (data-instruction separation) both fails to detect attacks that operate through contextual manipulation and degrades contextually appropriate behavior. We then recast prompt injection via the lens of Contextual Integrity (CI), a privacy theory that judges information flow compliance with contextual norms. This explains types of attacks that current defenses attempt to patch and predict advanced ones future agents will face. We develop unique benign and attack scenarios that force an agent to violate the norms by (1) misrepresenting the flow, (2) manipulating norms, or (3) mixing multiple flows. This reframing suggests an impossibility argument: an adversary can always construct a context under which a blocked flow appears legitimate, or a defender who tightens norms will block genuinely legitimate flows. Our findings suggest that current research addresses a shrinking fraction of future attack surfaces. Instead, through CI, we offer a principled framework for evaluating context-sensitive failures, and designing CI-aware alignment for frontier autonomous agents.

3e356d5fb8107d7e4a2ee8a3.title_original: EduSOC: A Lightweight Simulated Security Operations Center with AI Incident Responders
3e356d5fb8107d7e4a2ee8a3.excerpt: arXiv:2605.17703v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents EduSOC, a lightweight web-based Security Operations Center (SOC) simulation platform for cybersecurity education. Conventional cyber ranges can be complex and resource-intensive to deploy, particularly for introductory exercises focused on investigative decision-making rather than infrastructure configuration. EduSOC provides an alternative by combining continuous synthetic event generation, searchable supporting evidence, and role-based artificial intelligence (AI) responders that assist investigations without revealing underlying incident classifications. Students remain responsible for interpreting evidence, consulting simulated operational teams, and justifying their escalation decisions. A preliminary classroom evaluation was conducted across three university cohorts, comprising 50 matched pre- and post-simulation survey participants. The findings indicated high student engagement and improvements in self-reported SOC self-efficacy, while short-term knowledge gains varied across cohorts. These findings provide empirical insight into the use of lightweight, AI-supported SOC simulations in university cybersecurity education.

7f4d4d9cad05b3fbbaf3045c.title_original: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment
7f4d4d9cad05b3fbbaf3045c.excerpt: arXiv:2606.25750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Repeated safety evaluation of open-weight large language models requires generating and judging responses for many related checkpoints. We introduce RAS (Refusal Alignment Score), a representation-based, reference-relative indicator of harmful-request refusal computed by the five-stage SafeVec procedure. SafeVec extracts layer-wise refusal directions from an aligned reference model, measures their alignment in related targets, and calibrates a score from 0 to 100 using behavioral attack success rates (ASR) from reference and calibration models. Subsequent target scoring uses input forward passes alone. Across 18 held-out variants from the Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families, RAS correlates with $100(1-\mathrm{ASR})$ (Pearson 0.934, Spearman 0.851) and achieves 83.0% pairwise ordering agreement. Across five prompt configurations for the Llama reference, directions have mean cosine similarity 0.939. With calibration ASR already available, setup-inclusive evaluation of five targets achieves a speedup of 3.2 to 80.5 times over the specified behavioral protocol. These results support refusal alignment as an efficient signal for screening related checkpoints and prioritizing behavioral audits.

f856c928bb1fa6e8f3719650.title_original: A Re-Keying Game for Encrypted Multi-Agent Control under Persistent Threats
f856c928bb1fa6e8f3719650.excerpt: arXiv:2607.12742v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) lets a coordinator control a fleet on encrypted states, but CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic, returns noisy decryptions from which an adversary can recover the secret key. Flooding each decryption with noise defends it, but a fleet must decrypt to act, so the count of decryptions grows every cycle while the loop tolerates only bounded noise. We formulate the choice of flooding and key lifetime as a leader-follower game between the fleet operator and an advanced persistent threat that listens first and then spoofs the agents' sensors. We show that the closed loop decides how long a key may be used: the formation's specification caps each key's decryption budget through the loop's $H_2$ norm, and only re-keying, not bootstrapping, renews it. A spoof consumes part of the specification that flooding needs, and the coordination graph and the cost of an alarm decide in closed form whether the scan alone, a lower flood or nothing deters it. On 196 agents escorting a convoy at 128-bit security, five graphs with the same spectral radius differ 18-fold in key lifetime, a lower flood deters the spoofer on the torus for a twentieth of a key a day, and on the ring it cuts the damage 7 times. More broadly, any system that must repeatedly decrypt to act has a key lifetime set by its tolerance to noise, making key management part of control design.

ab42752b05fe010a10cd28bf.title_original: TaintRadar: Semantic-Aware Taint-Style Vulnerability Detection via Augmented Code Property Graphs
ab42752b05fe010a10cd28bf.excerpt: arXiv:2607.16456v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite significant advances, static vulnerability analysis suffers from three critical limitations: coarse sanitization modeling (treating validation as a binary barrier), database blindness (breaking taint tracking across persistence layers), and shallow object-oriented analysis (missing field-level and interprocedural data flows). These flaws stem from a common root cause: Code Property Graph (CPG)-based taint analyses lack a compositional semantic layer to jointly model sanitization, persistence, and object aliasing. Consequently, existing tools generate excessive false positives or miss critical attack paths entirely. To address these limitations, we present TaintRadar, an approach that systematically augments CPGs with three independent semantic analysis layers. First, vulnerability-typed sanitization computes node-level safety guarantees using transfer functions and context-sensitive parameter binding. Second, persistence-aware propagation integrates database schema constraints and query safety analysis to track multi-script attack paths traversing shared database states. Finally, object-aware reaching definitions combine calling and bounded variable alias contexts to precisely model object-field mutations across method boundaries. We evaluate TaintRadar on synthetic benchmarks and real-world systems. On the SARD benchmark, TaintRadar reduces false positives while maintaining 83 percent overall accuracy. Across 19 rea

9713bfc5a0f667d0956e99a8.title_original: A Maximum Entropy Implementation of Differential Privacy Under Linear Invariants
9713bfc5a0f667d0956e99a8.excerpt: arXiv:2607.22450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Differential privacy is the standard for ensuring data privacy and is widely used in major data publications, including reporting results from the U.S. decennial census. Common implementation of differential privacy uses independent Gaussian or Laplace noise addition to the database. However, there could be aggregate (linear) queries to the database that are excluded from the privacy budget, for example, state totals that can not be perturbed due to constitutional mandates. Any implementation of a differential privacy is required to honor these constraints, also referred to as invariants. Under aggregation constraints, the noise vector is no longer independent and the traditional differential privacy guarantees have to be re-evaluated. We propose a high entropy differential privacy implementation that maintains the aggregation invariants with probability one or exponentially close to one and derive the privacy guarantees for the implementation under the invariants. The theoretical proof also gives a solution to an open question about the null space of correlation matrices. Moreover, the methodology has general use in the context of sampling from normal mixture models under linear equality constraints.

bf3778f2a49a2a1517f1b6dc.title_original: GAZEleak: Passcode Inference Against Eye-tracking XR Devices Through External Observation
bf3778f2a49a2a1517f1b6dc.excerpt: arXiv:2609.35040v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mixed-reality headsets such as Apple Vision Pro replace the touch screen with gaze-as-pointer interaction: the wearer looks at a target and confirms with an air pinch. Because the display is inside the headset and the eye tracker is walled off from third-party software, such input is widely assumed to be unobservable to bystanders, a built-in defense against the shoulder-surfing that plagues phones and laptops. We present GAZEleak, a side-channel attack that recovers gaze-driven input from external video of head motion alone, under a strictly local, physical-observer threat model: the adversary only films the wearer from across the room and installs no software on the device. The attack exploits the centrally coupled eye-head motor program: gaze shifts recruit small, target-dependent head reorientations that project into sub-degree pose changes recoverable from commodity video. GAZEleak implements a measurement-based, sparse-optical-flow inference pipeline for users' 6-digit device passcodes. On a preliminary front-view dataset from three author-subjects who were aware of the attack hypothesis, GAZEleak places the true code within the top ten guesses for 56% (10 of 18) of test codes under a cross-person protocol with no labeled victim data, and for every code of the most exposed subject. The performance is subject-dependent: no passcode from the least exposed subject reaches the top ten, although its median guessed passcode

3c47b939bbd894fc0b84501d.title_original: A Systematic Study of Security Enforcement at Android Inter-Component Boundaries
3c47b939bbd894fc0b84501d.excerpt: arXiv:2610.13597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Android's inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms (Activities, Services, BroadcastReceivers, ContentProviders, and URI scheme handlers) form the primary interface between applications and between applications and the system. We present a systematic study of security enforcement comprising 120 evaluations (99 inter-component interface evaluations across five interface categories, 10 platform security-control evaluations, and 11 dedicated positive controls) in over 30 Google and AOSP packages on Android 17 (API 37). Using an expected-versus-observed framework under a zero-permission attacker model, we evaluate whether each boundary's enforcement mechanism functions as designed. We find 97 enforcement gaps (80.8%) and 23 enforcement holds (19.2%). From these observations, we derive a 14-category enforcement gap taxonomy organized across manifest, code, platform, and architectural layers. Within our purposively selected corpus, observed enforcement outcomes differ substantially across interface categories: evaluated Activities and BroadcastReceivers exhibit a 100% gap rate, while ContentProviders, which benefit from framework-provided defenses such as setStrict(), achieve a 27.6% holds rate. We find that all seven evaluated platform compatibility changes with security intent are either disabled or gated at a targetSdkVersion that none of the applications in our evaluated corpus targets. 889b64ecc67b60d45fe4a4de.title_original: AI Security Literacy: Ecosystem-Based Competency Framework and K-12 Learning Platform
889b64ecc67b60d45fe4a4de.excerpt: arXiv:2610.28859v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adoption of artificial intelligence in K-12 schools has outpaced guidance for students, teachers, and administrators. Existing AI-literacy frameworks emphasize understanding and use; cybersecurity frameworks predate AI-specific threats, and neither defines AI security literacy as a competency domain in its own right. We propose an AI Security Literacy (AISL) framework of six dimensions spanning the school ecosystem, ground its technical dimensions in public AI-safety benchmarks and a reproducible multi-seed adversarial evaluation, and ground its attitudinal dimensions in nationally representative survey micro-data from U.S. teachers and adults. Only 34.5% of teachers report a school AI policy, and teachers see their own AI use as easing their work but students' use as complicating it; on the technical side, a reported robustness figure depends as much on the attack and the particular trained model as on the system evaluated. NeuralFortify, a browser-based K-12 platform built on real AI models, is presented as an illustrative operationalization.

ea07cf556c510d23790c5c58.title_original: Reconstructing False Alarm and Detection Rates in Quantum Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection
ea07cf556c510d23790c5c58.excerpt: arXiv:2610.35235v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Published results in quantum machine learning for intrusion detection (QML-IDS) require joint interpretation of false-positive rate (FPR), attack true-positive rate (TPR), and evaluation provenance. We reconstruct operating points in the 25-entry frame selected by Kaissar and colleagues: 21 included articles, 20 identified documentary families, substantive methodological material consulted for 15, and 24 descriptive points from five. In one test-labelled comparison, a quantum support vector machine reduces FPR from 6.875% for random forest to 3.329%, while TPR decreases from 93.955% to 93.682%; both rates improve against three other comparators. In another study, a complete benign row identifies FPR as 12/6000 (0.200%), despite incomplete attack-side allocation that requires additional assumptions for TPR. Normalized matrices identify detection ranges rather than a unique aggregate rate. A uniform provenance rule separates training-described and test-adjusted results from six conditional illustrations whose independence remains unverified. The contribution is a reproducible interpretation of favorable comparisons and detection trade-offs, without converting descriptive results or hypothetical calculations into operational guarantees.

f7320f8621527a3c730a5a3a.title_original: Fooling Relying Parties of the EUDI Wallet Architecture: Credential Pooling Attacks and CRESTA, a Standard-Compliant Countermeasure
f7320f8621527a3c730a5a3a.excerpt: arXiv:2610.41655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The European Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet will let millions of EU citizens prove who they are and what they are entitled to, disclosing only what is needed. Many services need several credentials at once, such as an identity card and a university degree, so combined presentations are essential. We present credential pooling attacks on relying parties of the EUDI Wallet reference architecture. Colluding users, each holding some credentials in their own wallet, cooperate through a proxy that acts as a single synthetic user and presents all the requested credentials, although no single user holds them all. Every signature is genuine and computed by certified hardware, and nothing is extracted or forged. We ran the attack against the European Commission's reference implementation, also on two Android phones. The attack would fail if all credentials of a user carried the same public key, but colluding relying parties could then link all presentations of that user. For this reason, the Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF) requires a fresh key for each credential and recommends batches of single-use copies, each with its own key: precisely what makes pooling possible. One might think that preventing pooling requires giving up unlinkability or adopting non-standard cryptography, such as zero-knowledge proofs. We show that this is not the case: we present CRESTA (CREdential STApling), an efficient countermeasure that uses onl

30105c2655f03adbfe7be9c9.title_original: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense
30105c2655f03adbfe7be9c9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is widely used to customize large language models, but third-party adapters create supply-chain backdoor risks with under 1% modified parameters. Recent analytical null-space and subspace projection defenses report near-zero static Attack Success Rates (ASR), equating static silence with erasure. We audit subspace-projection defenses across four scales (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B), three architectures (Qwen2.5, InternLM2.5-1.8B, Spark-X2.6-4B), and five trigger families (suffix, natural phrase, prefix/in-sentence, double-negation syntax, and composite triggers). Statically, module-wise rank-1 trigger-difference projection cuts ASR from 60.4% to 0.0% on standard suites and 70.3% to 0.0% on 1,000 uncontaminated prompts (p = 3.055e-299) in under 5 s. By Theorem 1 (11,880/11,880 module-sample pairs), low-rank bottleneck amplification aligns benign polite-suffix probes with u_1(B) (median cosine 0.8934-0.9705), reaching 0.0% ASR without trigger knowledge. However, static suppression is not erasure. Under 5-sample reactivation, single-round weight-editing baselines rebound to 91.7%-100.0% ASR in Epoch 1 (Fine-Pruning, ANP, NEEDLE, LoRA-Patch; 48.7% for single-round dual projection) and 100.0% by Epoch 2. Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 prove single-sided projection leaves non-zero gradients along u_1 across 168/168 modules (27.2x-31.1x above random expectation), while Haar orthogonal rotation shows Epoch-2 immuni

2f65ce45b48d35d870eae8b1.title_original: EDGChain-E: A Decentralized Git-Based Framework for Versioning Encrypted Energy Data
2f65ce45b48d35d870eae8b1.excerpt: arXiv:2507.01615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper proposes a new decentralized framework, named EDGChain-E (Encrypted-Data-Git Chain for Energy), designed to manage version-controlled, encrypted energy data using blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System. The framework incorporates a Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) to orchestrate collaborative data governance across the lifecycle of energy research and operations, such as smart grid monitoring, demand forecasting, and peer-to-peer energy trading. In EDGChain-E, initial commits capture the full encrypted datasets-such as smart meter readings or grid telemetry-while subsequent updates are tracked as encrypted Git patches, ensuring integrity, traceability, and privacy. This versioning mechanism supports secure collaboration across multiple stakeholders (e.g., utilities, researchers, regulators) without compromising sensitive or regulated information. We highlight the framework's capability to maintain FAIR-compliant (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) provenance of encrypted data. By embedding hash-based content identifiers in Merkle trees, the system enables transparent, auditable, and immutable tracking of data changes, thereby supporting reproducibility and trust in decentralized energy applications.

8be5824412ae0e206d972e68.title_original: NL-SME: Enhancing Multi-Step Gradient Inversion through Adaptive Two-State Matching
8be5824412ae0e206d972e68.excerpt: arXiv:2509.22082v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training among multiple clients without directly sharing their raw data.However, gradient inversion attacks can exploit the model updates exchanged during training to reconstruct clients' private data.With multiple local training steps, an observed update combines gradients evaluated at changing model states and potentially different mini-batches, while intermediate states remain hidden. Restricting gradient evaluation to a single state on the segment between the initial and final models can exclude states that better fit the accumulated update.We consider reconstruction from an individual client's endpoint models, assuming that the training labels are known.We propose NL-SME, a regularized two-state gradient surrogate for matching multi-step client updates without replaying local training.The surrogate adapts its evaluation center, regularizes its displacement, and averages raw parameter gradients at two shared symmetric states.We evaluate NL-SME against existing gradient inversion methods on FEMNIST and CIFAR-100 with varying numbers of local training steps.The results show improved reconstruction quality, highlighting the privacy risks of sharing individual client updates after multiple local steps.

96e87771de41514c418fb075.title_original: On the Price of Privacy for Language Identification and Generation
96e87771de41514c418fb075.excerpt: arXiv:2604.07238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models train on sensitive user data, so we ask what differential privacy (DP) costs in language learning. We study private language identification and generation in the agnostic statistical setting. For identification, privacy is free: at every fixed $\varepsilon$, pure DP and $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP with $\delta\ge n^{-O(1)}$ keep the non-private rate $\exp(-r(n))$ for every $r(n)=o(n)$. For generation, the price depends on what is public. With a public witness bound, pure DP loses at most a factor $\Theta(\min\{1,\varepsilon\})$ in the exponent, and on suitable two-language collections the optimal rate is $\exp(-\Theta(\min\{1,\varepsilon\}\,n))$. Without such a bound, pure DP can lose the exponential rate itself, already for two languages: every rate $\exp(-o(n))$ stays achievable, but no exponential rate is. On these collections, $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP keeps an exponential rate if and only if $\log(1/\delta)=o(n)$. Three facts about pure DP drive the proofs. It turns a robustness margin into an exponentially small error. It obeys a private form of Le Cam's two-point bound. And it cannot see the absence of a string.

d6967a318368eb6520cf8dba.title_original: Not What a Child Expressed: Auditing the Sign-to-Text Safety Interface in Child-Facing AI
d6967a318368eb6520cf8dba.excerpt: arXiv:2610.07519v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automatic sign language translation (SLT) has entered consumer products, turning American Sign Language into English text for dictation, messaging, and queries put to a conversational assistant. Child-facing AI and platform trust-and-safety tooling decide on text, using filters on minor accounts and grooming classifiers that score chat messages. A signing child who uses SLT therefore reaches these safeguards through a translation. We found no publicly documented system in which the two have been jointly evaluated, and the leading deployed SLT model was neither trained nor formally evaluated on signers under 18. Errors that alter negation, participant roles, secrecy, urgency or help-seeking could change a safety decision without disturbing fluency. This paper proposes a Deaf-informed pre-deployment audit of that boundary, with a failure taxonomy, a sanitised scenario schema, four comparison conditions, and four outcome measures. Auslan is the planned first case study.

def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.title_original: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.02376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that exploits the capability of emerging on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. Unlike existing solutions, AltoPIR achieves high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. However, the on-CPU accelerator has only a few small registers and shares its core with request handling. As a result, it runs far below its peak rate while its operands arrive from memory, and it remains idle while its core handles requests. To keep the accelerator busy, we design mechanisms that reduce both the memory traffic of a batch and the core cycles spent on each request. Our experimental results show that AltoPIR outperforms existing CPU-based solutions by up to 50.1x.

0d680795ed090de32a832e53.title_original: 텐센트 'Hy4 플래시' 출시...일상 업무 특화·작업 비용 95% 절감
0d680795ed090de32a832e53.excerpt: 텐센트가 문서 작성과 프레젠테이션 제작, 자료 조사 등 일상적인 업무에 특화한 저비용 AI 모델을 선보였다. 자체 평가에서 기존 모델보다 작업당 비용을 최대 95% 줄이면서도 사용자 만족도는 앤트로픽의 '클로드 하이쿠 5.5'에 근접한 수준을 기록했다.텐센트는 16일(현지시간) 'Hy4 플래시(Hy4 flash)'를 출시했다. 지난 4일 공개한 대형 모델 'Hy4'의 성능을 이어받으면서 일반적인 업무 처리에 필요한 비용과 시간을 줄이는 데 초점을 맞춘 모델이다.전체 매개변수 2240억개 가운데 토큰당 120억개만 활성화하는 전문가
0d680795ed090de32a832e53.title_ko: 텐센트, 업무용 ‘Hy4 플래시’ 출시…자체 평가서 작업 비용 최대 95% 절감
0d680795ed090de32a832e53.summary_ko: 텐센트가 문서 작성·자료 조사·프레젠테이션 제작 등 일상 업무용 AI 모델 ‘Hy4 플래시’를 출시했다. 최대 100만 토큰 문맥과 멀티모달 입력을 지원하며, 자체 평가에서 기존 Hy4 대비 작업당 비용을 최대 95% 줄였다고 밝혔다. 내부 직원 대상 평가에서는 ‘클로드 하이쿠 5.5’와 비슷한 사용자 만족도를 기록했다고 설명했다.
0d680795ed090de32a832e53.background_ko: 복잡한 추론용 대형 Hy4와 별도로 반복적인 일상 업무의 처리 시간과 비용을 줄이려는 제품 전략에 따라 개발됐다.

curation.reason_ko: 텐센트가 일상 업무용 저비용 모델을 출시했으며 비용 절감 수치는 자체 평가에 근거한다.

baee7199808e674ec9a2805c.title_original: 메타, AI로 코드 오류 사전 차단...개인정보 관련 심각한 버그 74건 발견
baee7199808e674ec9a2805c.excerpt: 메타가 AI를 활용해 소프트웨어 오류를 사전에 찾아내는 테스트 시스템을 도입해 올해 상반기에만 개인정보 관련 심각한 버그 74건을 발견했다. 같은 기간 개인정보 관련 중대 사고도 20% 감소했으며, AI가 직접 테스트 코드를 작성하고 실행해 오류를 검증하는 방식이다.메타는 지난달 29일(현지시간) 자체 개발한 AI 테스트 시스템 '캐칭 지트테스트(Catching JiTTests)'를 실제 인프라에 적용한 결과를 공개했다.이 기술은 개발자가 수정한 코드에서 발생할 수 있는 오류를 찾아내기 위해 AI가 직접 테스트 코드를 작성하고 실행
baee7199808e674ec9a2805c.title_ko: 메타, AI 테스트로 개인정보 관련 심각한 버그 74건 사전 발견
baee7199808e674ec9a2805c.summary_ko: 메타는 AI가 코드 변경 전후의 동작 차이를 확인하는 실행형 테스트를 생성하는 ‘Catching JiTTests’의 운영 성과를 공개했다. 회사에 따르면 상반기에 개인정보 관련 심각한 버그 74건을 서비스 반영 전에 발견했으며, 엔지니어가 보고한 실제 오류 적중률은 60%였다. 외부 개발자용 코드나 API는 공개하지 않았다.
baee7199808e674ec9a2805c.background_ko: 기존 테스트나 AI 코드 검토에서 놓칠 수 있는 오류를 실제 실행으로 확인하고, 빨라진 코드 작성·배포 속도에 맞춰 검증을 강화하려는 취지다.

curation.reason_ko: 메타가 AI 테스트로 개인정보 관련 중대 버그 74건을 찾았다고 밝혀 실무 방어 활용 사례를 제시했다.

af3b307a98ade0f3a6154779.title_original: [배종찬의 보안 빅데이터] 통신차단까지 무력화된 수능 AI 부정행위 우려
af3b307a98ade0f3a6154779.title_ko: AI 기기 활용 시험 부정행위 우려…칼럼서 감독·통신 차단의 한계 지적
af3b307a98ade0f3a6154779.summary_ko: AI 안경·초소형 카메라·이어폰과 생성형 AI를 결합한 시험 부정행위가 감독 체계와 공정성에 미칠 위험을 다룬 칼럼이다. 필자는 육안 감독과 통신 차단만으로는 대응에 한계가 있다며, 주변 통신망 장애와 오프라인 기기 사용 가능성까지 고려한 대책을 촉구했다.
af3b307a98ade0f3a6154779.background_ko: 국가 자격시험에서 첨단 기기를 동원한 부정행위가 드러난 것이 수능 공정성 우려의 배경으로 제시됐다.

b3ff44c2617709b2238cff61.title_original: Court clears brothers of $25 million Ethereum crypto heist charges
b3ff44c2617709b2238cff61.excerpt: US District Judge Jessica Clarke has acquitted two brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency in about 12 seconds through a scheme that exploited a bug in the Ethereum blockchain. [...]
b3ff44c2617709b2238cff61.title_ko: 이더리움 2,500만 달러 탈취 혐의 형제에 무죄 선고
b3ff44c2617709b2238cff61.summary_ko: 미 연방법원이 이더리움 취약점을 악용해 약 2,500만 달러를 탈취한 혐의로 기소된 형제에게 무죄를 선고했다. 법원은 검찰이 통신사기죄 성립에 필요한 중대한 허위 진술을 입증하지 못했다고 판단했다. MEV-Boost 릴레이 취약점 악용과 거래 순서 조작은 검찰이 제기한 혐의다.
b3ff44c2617709b2238cff61.background_ko: 법원은 검찰이 범행 실행 과정에서 중대한 허위 진술이 있었다는 점을 입증하지 못해 통신사기 등 혐의의 유죄를 뒷받침할 증거가 부족하다고 판단했다.

CVE-2024-58407.description: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.1 contain a global buffer over-read vulnerability in DecodeSignificantRun() in image/decode/segdec.c due to an unchecked run length. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file with an out-of-range iMaxRun value that indexes gSignificantRunBin[] out of bounds, causing memory disclosure or crashes during decoding.

CVE-2024-58408.description: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.1 contain a global buffer over-read vulnerability in initLookupTables() in image/decode/strdec.c caused by an unchecked bit depth index. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file with an out-of-range bit depth in the image header to read beyond the cbChannels array, causing crashes or memory disclosure.

CVE-2025-5809.description: An improper privilege management vulnerability in an LDAP extension used with OpenText eDirectory could require a technical or proxy user to be granted write permission to the ACL when only permission to modify a specific LDAP attribute is intended. A user who possesses the proxy user's credentials could use the excessive ACL permission to modify access rights for objects within the affected container, potentially resulting in unauthorized elevation of privilege. The issue is addressed in OpenText eDirectory 25.2.

CVE-2026-127043.description: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the myGESTIÓN Time Tracking module. The server skips the permission check when processing the “worker” parameter. By modifying this parameter, an authenticated user can view other users' time logs, including those of administrators.

CVE-2026-127044.description: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the STEL Order Tempo module. The server retrieves data based on the `empleadoId` parameter without checking the user's permissions. By modifying this parameter, an authenticated user can view the first name, last name, role, job title, and vacation days of other employees.

CVE-2026-129851.description: SeaweedFS before 4.42 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the VolumeServer.FetchAndWriteNeedle gRPC method that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the incomplete CVE-2026-73080 fix. Attackers can supply crafted replicas[].url entries or an azure_endpoint to make the volume server send requests with controlled tokens and bodies to internal services and metadata addresses.
CVE-2026-129851.summary_ko: SeaweedFS 4.42 이전 버전의 VolumeServer.FetchAndWriteNeedle gRPC 메서드에 서버 측 요청 위조 취약점이 있다. 인증되지 않은 공격자가 볼륨 서버를 통해 내부 서비스와 메타데이터 주소로 토큰과 본문이 조작된 요청을 보내게 할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129851.background_ko: CVE-2026-73080 수정이 불완전하며, 복제본 URL이나 Azure 엔드포인트 값으로 서버의 요청 대상을 제어할 수 있다.

CVE-2026-129852.description: SeaweedFS before 4.42 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to probe local files by supplying a filesystem path in gcs_google_application_credentials. Attackers can send crafted gRPC FetchAndWriteNeedle requests and use differing error messages to learn file existence, readability, and partial content shape on the host.

CVE-2026-129853.description: LimeSurvey before 6.17.16+260814 and 7.x before 7.0.10+260813 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the public statistics page via POST parameter names. Attackers can submit backtick-containing parameter names to buildSelects() and use blind techniques to read administrator password hashes and survey responses on MySQL or MariaDB.

CVE-2026-129854.description: RedAmon 4.0.0 before 7.8.0 contains a missing object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to control other tenants' agent sessions by supplying arbitrary session ids. Attackers can call /api/agent/sessions, interact and kill routes to list, kill, or send commands into other users' meterpreter and shell sessions on their compromised targets.
CVE-2026-129854.summary_ko: RedAmon 4.0.0 이상 7.8.0 미만 버전에서 인증된 사용자가 다른 테넌트의 에이전트 세션을 제어할 수 있다. 다른 사용자의 meterpreter·셸 세션을 조회·종료하거나 명령을 보낼 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129854.background_ko: 에이전트 세션에 대한 객체 수준 권한 검사가 없어 임의의 세션 ID로 다른 테넌트의 세션에 접근할 수 있다.

CVE-2026-129855.description: RedAmon before 7.8.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the kali-sandbox terminal server that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain a root shell by connecting to its WebSocket listener on port 8016. Attackers who can reach the port from co-resident containers or the host loopback can send keystrokes to an interactive /bin/bash session, executing commands as root inside the kali-sandbox container.

CVE-2026-129856.description: wallabag 2.3.3 before 2.6.16 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through article author metadata rendered with Twig raw in entry.html.twig. Attackers can embed HTML event handlers in a web page's author metadata so scripts run in a victim's wallabag session when the saved entry is opened, exposing their data.

CVE-2026-129857.description: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.1 contain a heap buffer overflow in ReadBinaryData() in jxrgluelib/JXRMeta.c caused by integer overflow of the metadata count. Attackers can supply a JPEG XR file with a count of 0xFFFFFFFE or 0xFFFFFFFF, wrapping PKAlloc(uCount + 2) to an undersized buffer that the following file read overflows, corrupting heap memory in decoding applications.
CVE-2026-129857.summary_ko: Microsoft jxrlib 1.1 이하와 mircomir jxrlib 포크 1.3.1 미만에 힙 버퍼 오버플로 취약점이 있다. 조작된 JPEG XR 파일로 디코딩 애플리케이션의 힙 메모리가 손상될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129857.background_ko: 메타데이터 개수의 정수 오버플로로 너무 작은 버퍼가 할당되고, 뒤이은 파일 읽기가 버퍼 범위를 넘는다.

CVE-2026-129858.description: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.6 contain a stack buffer over-read vulnerability in ReadWMIHeader() in image/decode/strdec.c due to an unterminated signature buffer. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file whose 8 signature bytes contain no zero byte, causing strstr to read past the stack buffer and potentially crash the application.

CVE-2026-129859.description: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.1 contain a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in ImageStrDecDecode() in image/decode/strdec.c. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file declaring a colour format with no channels, leaving p1MBbuffer[0] NULL and crashing the decoder via memset.

CVE-2026-129860.description: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.7 contain a reachable assertion vulnerability in ParsePFDEntry() that allows attackers to abort applications via an invalid orientation tag. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file with an out-of-range WMP_tagTransformation value to crash applications using default assertion-enabled builds, or store an unchecked orientation value otherwise.

CVE-2026-129861.description: @tinacms/graphql 2.2.2 through 4.1.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the content root by following pre-existing dangling symlinks. Attackers can create documents through the GraphQL API targeting a dangling symlink, bypassing assertWithinBase checks, to write controlled content such as authorized_keys to server-writable locations.

CVE-2026-129862.description: Koillection before 1.8.6 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view objects nested under private parents through the shared search autocomplete route. Attackers can query GET /user/{username}/search/autocomplete/{term}, whose native SQL filters on visibility instead of final_visibility, to obtain names, ids and counts of hidden collections, items, albums and wishlists.

CVE-2026-129863.description: GitBucket through 4.48.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to edit and merge other users' pull requests because the PATCH pulls and PUT pulls merge REST API endpoints only check read access. Attackers can close, reopen, retitle, retarget, or merge pull requests into the base branch without write permission on public repositories or as private-repository guest collaborators.
CVE-2026-129863.summary_ko: GitBucket 4.48.0 이하에서 인증된 사용자가 쓰기 권한 없이 다른 사용자의 풀 리퀘스트를 수정하거나 기준 브랜치에 병합할 수 있다. 공개 저장소 또는 게스트 협업자로 참여한 비공개 저장소에서 악용할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129863.background_ko: 풀 리퀘스트 수정·병합 REST API가 읽기 권한만 확인한다.

CVE-2026-129864.description: Frappe CRM before 1.84.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the get_deal_contacts method that allows authenticated low-privileged users to read contacts of deals they cannot access. Attackers can supply or iterate CRM Deal names to obtain linked contacts' full names, email addresses, and mobile numbers, bypassing row-level permission rules.

CVE-2026-129865.description: Dinky through 1.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in DataSourceController.testConnect that allows any authenticated user to open arbitrary JDBC connections by supplying caller-controlled connection settings. Attackers can probe internal hosts and ports via returned driver errors, or supply a MySQL JDBC URL enabling local-infile against a malicious server to read files from the Dinky host.

CVE-2026-129866.description: Dinky through 1.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ClusterConfigurationController that allows authenticated users without cluster configuration permissions to list Flink cluster configurations. Attackers can query the /api/clusterConfiguration/list and listAll endpoints to retrieve full configJson deployment settings for every cluster in their tenant.

CVE-2026-129867.description: Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject script by abusing #topic link wrapping in preparePost and parsePostTag. Attackers can publish posts or comments with a crafted topic containing a lone '<' and event handler to steal the PAOPAO_TOKEN JWT from localStorage and take over viewer accounts.

CVE-2026-129868.description: Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 fails to validate the attachment_price field when creating posts, allowing authenticated users to set negative prices on charge attachments. Attackers with two ordinary accounts can download the attachment via GET /v1/attachment, where the negative price increases the buyer's wallet balance, minting funds to purchase other users' paid attachments.

CVE-2026-129869.description: SamWaf 1.0.128 through 1.3.25-beta.11 contains a request body inspection bypass vulnerability in WafEngine.ServeHTTP that skips bodies with chunked encoding or lengths of 2048 bytes or more. Remote unauthenticated attackers can send SQL injection, XSS, command injection, traversal or upload payloads chunked or padded, which reach the protected backend uninspected.

CVE-2026-129870.description: Rocboss paopao-ce 0.2.0 through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a path traversal vulnerability in LocalOSS DeleteObject that allows authenticated users to delete arbitrary files by submitting crafted media values. Attackers can send dot-dot-slash sequences in the avatar or media content to POST /v1/user/avatar or POST /v1/post/comment, deleting server-writable files including configuration and data.

CVE-2026-129871.description: Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a payment bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain paid attachments by reading storage URLs from the GET /v1/post endpoint. Attackers can download the paid file directly from the unauthenticated LocalOSS /oss static route, whose signed URL expired parameter is never checked.

CVE-2026-129872.description: REBUILD 2.7.0 through 4.5.4 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject AjQL conditions through the plan parameter of /project/tasks/list. Attackers can use priority-* plans and the returned task count as a boolean oracle to recover a task creator's SHA-256 password hash and log in as that user, including the administrator.

CVE-2026-129873.description: REBUILD 4.3.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to obtain a SYSTEM_USER token by requesting /commons/file-preview with an arbitrary src value. Attackers can read the leaked _csrfToken from the redirect Location header and send it as X-AuthToken to access the admin center and administrative APIs.
CVE-2026-129873.summary_ko: REBUILD 4.3.0~4.5.4에 권한 상승 취약점이 있다. 낮은 권한의 인증된 사용자가 파일 미리보기 기능에서 유출되는 SYSTEM_USER 토큰을 얻어 관리자 센터와 관리 API에 접근할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129873.background_ko: 파일 미리보기 응답의 리디렉션 Location 헤더로 SYSTEM_USER의 _csrfToken이 유출되며, 이 값이 인증 토큰으로 사용될 수 있다.

CVE-2026-129874.description: REBUILD 3.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify their own roleId through mass assignment in /app/entity/record-save and /app/entity/common-save. Attackers can submit their own User record with roleId set to the built-in administrator role, bypassing updatable=false restrictions to gain full administrator privileges.
CVE-2026-129874.summary_ko: REBUILD 3.5.0~4.5.4에 권한 상승 취약점이 있다. 낮은 권한의 인증된 사용자가 자신의 사용자 레코드에 있는 역할 정보를 변경해 완전한 관리자 권한을 얻을 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129874.background_ko: 사용자 레코드 저장 시 대량 할당으로 roleId를 변경할 수 있으며, updatable=false 제한이 우회된다.

CVE-2026-129875.description: REBUILD 4.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to recover the administrator password hash by filtering User.password through the MCP QueryRecords tool. Attackers can send LK2 prefix-match filters to the /gw/mcp/sse gateway and use the returned total count as an oracle to extract the SHA-256 hash one character at a time, then log in as administrator.
CVE-2026-129875.summary_ko: REBUILD 4.5.0~4.5.4의 정보 노출 취약점으로 낮은 권한의 인증된 사용자가 MCP QueryRecords 도구를 통해 관리자 비밀번호의 SHA-256 해시를 복원하고 관리자 계정으로 로그인할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129875.background_ko: MCP QueryRecords가 User.password 필터를 허용하고 일치 건수를 반환해 비밀번호 해시를 추론할 수 있는 정보를 노출한다.

CVE-2026-129876.description: OfficeCLI 1.0.56 through 1.0.161 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the officecli watch preview that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped numbering w:color values. Attackers can craft a DOCX whose color closes the style element, then abuse the unauthenticated /api/batch endpoint to read local files and modify the watched document.

CVE-2026-129877.description: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve server secrets through the /api/v1/config/defaults endpoint. Attackers can send a GET request to obtain the operator's LLM provider API keys and GitHub or GitLab tokens, then abuse those services and accessible repositories.
CVE-2026-129877.summary_ko: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1~3.8.0에서 인증 없이 서버 비밀정보를 조회할 수 있다. LLM 제공업체 API 키와 GitHub·GitLab 토큰이 유출돼 관련 서비스와 접근 가능한 저장소가 악용될 수 있다.

CVE-2026-129878.description: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in ReportGenerator.generate_task_report that allows registered users to read server files and perform SSRF. Attackers can create a project whose name contains a link attachment element and download the task PDF report to retrieve local files or internal network responses.

CVE-2026-129879.description: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write arbitrary files by importing projects with crafted IDs. Attackers can set absolute or ../ project IDs via /api/v1/database/import, then upload ZIPs through /api/v1/scan/upload-zip following cloned symlinks to overwrite app/main.py for remote code execution.
CVE-2026-129879.summary_ko: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1~3.8.0의 경로 순회 취약점으로 인증된 사용자가 임의 파일을 쓸 수 있다. 애플리케이션 파일을 덮어써 원격 코드를 실행할 수도 있다.
CVE-2026-129879.background_ko: 프로젝트 가져오기에서 절대 경로나 상위 디렉터리 경로를 포함한 ID가 허용되며, ZIP 업로드 시 복제된 심볼릭 링크를 따라 파일이 기록된다.

CVE-2026-129880.description: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows registered users to leak server-wide GitLab or Gitea tokens via repository_url. Attackers can create a gitlab or gitea project pointing to a controlled host and request its branches to capture the operator's token and reach internal hosts.

CVE-2026-129881.description: Weblate 2026.6 through 2026.11.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in ChangeManager.last_changes() that exposes workspaces the viewer cannot view by skipping Workspace.can_view() checks site-wide. Anonymous visitors on instances with REQUIRE_LOGIN disabled and only public projects can query /changes/, /api/changes/, or RSS/CSV feeds to obtain hidden workspace names, UUIDs, actions, and timestamps.

CVE-2026-129882.description: Kiwi TCMS before 17.1 contains a hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge signed data by using the publicly known Django SECRET_KEY in tcms/settings/common.py. Attackers can forge or tamper with signed cookie-based messages and django.core.signing payloads, weakening password-reset and session-authentication HMACs on deployments keeping the default.

CVE-2026-129883.description: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to send users to arbitrary sites by supplying an unvalidated redirectUri parameter on the /pay/[id] payment link page. Attackers can distribute payment links with a malicious redirectUri that PayPageWidget opens via window.open after payment without noopener, enabling phishing and reverse tabnabbing of the payment page.

CVE-2026-129884.description: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the fetchClientSecret Next.js server action that allows unauthenticated attackers to create Stripe checkout sessions for other teams. Attackers can invoke the action with a forged Team object containing a victim's stripeCustomerId to obtain Growth plan Checkout session client secrets with attacker-influenced return URLs.

CVE-2026-129885.description: Unrolled Secure before 1.18.0 contains an SSLRedirect bypass vulnerability in Secure.isSSL() that trusts the client-supplied r.URL.Scheme to determine HTTPS transport. Attackers can send plaintext HTTP requests with an absolute-form https:// request-target to skip the HTTPS redirect and have application responses served unencrypted.

CVE-2026-129886.description: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in revalidatePathAction and revalidateCacheTagAction server actions in revalidate.ts. Unauthenticated attackers can use action identifiers exposed in the client bundle to send POST requests that purge cached pages and data, forcing repeated regeneration and degrading performance.

CVE-2026-129887.description: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read non-public team metadata by requesting the team join page with any invite ID. Attackers who know a team slug can obtain the serialized Team object, exposing billing email, billing status, Stripe customer ID, verified domain and support identifiers.

CVE-2026-129888.description: Cetmix Tower through 17.0.3.0.0 and 18.0 before 18.0.4.0.1 contains an improper SSH host key verification vulnerability in SSHConnection.connect() that falls back to Paramiko's AutoAddPolicy when no host key is pinned. On-path attackers using ARP or DNS spoofing can present their own host key during Skip Host Key or Get from Host connections to capture stored SSH passwords and tamper with commands and files.

CVE-2026-129940.description: Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the unauthenticated GET /prime/redirect route that allows remote attackers to redirect users to external sites. Attackers can craft links with a 36-character id and arbitrary url parameter on the trusted Prime host to send victims to phishing sites.

CVE-2026-129941.description: Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register accounts via the createUser mutation on /prime/graphql. Because the isAuthenticated() guard has its check commented out and createAbility() hard-codes every role to admin, attackers can log in with full administrative control over content, users, webhooks and settings.
CVE-2026-129941.summary_ko: Prime CMS(@primecms/core) 0.4.0-beta.0 이하 버전에 인증 우회 취약점이 있다. 인증되지 않은 공격자가 계정을 등록하고 관리자 권한으로 로그인해 콘텐츠, 사용자, 웹훅, 설정을 제어할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129941.background_ko: isAuthenticated()의 인증 검사가 주석 처리되어 있고, createAbility()가 모든 역할을 관리자로 고정한다.

CVE-2026-129942.description: Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to invoke privileged GraphQL mutations because the @Authorized() decorator is omitted. Attackers can call updateWebhook, createRelease, unpublishDocument and updateUser at /prime/graphql to create releases and, with a record UUID, redirect webhooks, unpublish documents, or overwrite user profiles.

CVE-2026-129943.description: Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the updateSystem GraphQL mutation that allows authenticated administrators to execute shell commands via the package version string. Attackers can append shell metacharacters to the unvalidated version value, which is passed to child_process.exec() in yarn add or npm install commands, executing commands as the server process.

CVE-2026-129944.description: Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the getIsPathValid function that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access sibling paths sharing a content directory name prefix. Attackers can send requests with a no-cors header to the blob, update, and tree handlers under /api/keystatic to read, create, overwrite, or delete files such as posts-evil/pwn.yaml.

CVE-2026-129945.description: Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the githubOauthCallback handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to sign victims in with the attacker's GitHub account by omitting state validation. Attackers can induce victims to visit the OAuth callback with an attacker-obtained authorization code, causing victim edits in the admin UI to be committed under the attacker's GitHub identity.

CVE-2026-129946.description: Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the DocumentRenderer component that allows authenticated content editors to inject scripts via unvalidated link href values. Editors can paste anchors with javascript: URLs into document fields, executing script when visitors click rendered links and stealing the keystatic-gh-access-token cookie.

CVE-2026-129947.description: Contentlayer @contentlayer/core through 0.3.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JavaScript by embedding single quotes in content file names. Attackers can add a content file whose name breaks out of the import specifier in makeDataExportFile(), executing injected code when contentlayer dev or a Next.js dev server imports the generated module.

CVE-2026-129948.description: Contentlayer @contentlayer/source-files through 0.3.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers who control content files to execute JavaScript by abusing gray-matter's still-enabled JavaScript engine in parseMarkdown(). Attackers can start a Markdown or MDX file with a ---js or ---javascript frontmatter delimiter to run code during build, exposing CI build secrets.
CVE-2026-129948.summary_ko: Contentlayer의 @contentlayer/source-files 0.3.4 이하 버전에 코드 주입 취약점이 있다. 콘텐츠 파일을 제어하는 공격자가 빌드 중 JavaScript를 실행해 CI 빌드 비밀정보를 노출시킬 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129948.background_ko: parseMarkdown()에서 사용하는 gray-matter의 JavaScript 엔진이 활성화되어 있어 Markdown·MDX 프런트매터의 코드가 실행될 수 있다.

CVE-2026-129949.description: Rowy through 3.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to inject unsanitized HTML into Markdown cells. Attackers can store iframe, object, or form elements with javascript: URLs that execute when administrators view the table, stealing Firebase sessions.

CVE-2026-129950.description: Rowy through 3.0.0 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability in default Firebase Storage rules that grants any user holding a role read and write access to the entire bucket. Authenticated users restricted to a single table or read-only access can use the Firebase SDK directly to list, download, overwrite, and delete any stored files.

CVE-2026-129951.description: Rowy through 3.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to inject scripts via URL field links lacking scheme validation. Attackers can store values like javascript: URIs containing the string http in URL cells, executing script when victims click the open-link button to steal Firebase sessions.

CVE-2026-129952.description: NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain administrator access by forging JWTs with the hardcoded 'nodepress-secret' fallback key. Attackers can sign HS256 bearer tokens with the default issuer, audience, and role 'admin' to access administrator-only APIs for article, comment, options, and file management.
CVE-2026-129952.summary_ko: NodePress 8.5.1 이하 버전에는 인증 우회 취약점이 있다. 인증되지 않은 원격 공격자가 JWT를 위조해 관리자 권한을 얻고 게시글, 댓글, 옵션, 파일 관리용 관리자 API에 접근할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129952.background_ko: JWT 서명에 사용할 대체 비밀 키가 하드코딩되어 있어 공격자가 유효한 토큰을 위조할 수 있다.

CVE-2026-129953.description: NodePress through 8.5.1 contains a rate limit bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade throttling by spoofing the X-Forwarded-For header, because trustProxy is enabled. Attackers can send X-Forwarded-For set to 127.0.0.1 or rotate values to brute-force the administrator password via POST /admin/login and evade comment IP blocklists.

CVE-2026-129954.description: NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in linesToEmailContent() that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject markup into notification emails because comment content is not escaped. Attackers can post comments or replies via POST /comments containing forged links, images, or tracking resources rendered in administrator and author mail clients from the blog's address.

CVE-2026-129955.description: NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator access by using the hardcoded default password 'root'. Attackers can send base64-encoded 'root' to POST /admin/login when NP_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD is unset to obtain admin tokens and fully control the site.
CVE-2026-129955.summary_ko: NodePress 8.5.1 이하 버전에는 하드코딩된 기본 비밀번호로 인한 인증 우회 취약점이 있다. 관련 환경 변수가 설정되지 않은 경우 인증되지 않은 공격자가 관리자 토큰을 얻어 사이트를 완전히 제어할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129955.background_ko: NP_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD가 설정되지 않으면 하드코딩된 기본 관리자 비밀번호를 사용한다.

CVE-2026-129956.description: Sandboxie-Plus before 1.18.6 contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability in SbieSvc that allows standard users to launch UpdUtil.exe as SYSTEM via MSGID_PROCESS_RUN_UPDATER requests. Attackers can inject code into a signed SandMan.exe process to bypass the signature check and write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary paths, achieving SYSTEM code execution.
CVE-2026-129956.summary_ko: Sandboxie-Plus 1.18.6 이전 버전의 SbieSvc에 로컬 권한 상승 취약점이 있다. 일반 사용자가 서명 검사를 우회해 임의 경로에 파일을 쓰고 SYSTEM 권한으로 코드를 실행할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129956.background_ko: 서명된 SandMan.exe 프로세스에 주입된 코드로 SbieSvc의 서명 검사를 우회할 수 있다.

CVE-2026-129957.description: PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.0.0 before 9.2.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in back-office theme and module archive import that allows authenticated employees to write files outside intended directories. Attackers can craft a theme name in config/theme.yml or upload a module archive extracted before validation to place PHP files in web-accessible locations and execute code.
CVE-2026-129957.summary_ko: PrestaShop 8.2.9 미만 및 9.0.0 이상 9.2.1 미만의 백오피스 테마·모듈 압축 파일 가져오기에 경로 순회 취약점이 있다. 인증된 직원이 지정된 디렉터리 밖에 파일을 써 코드를 실행할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-129957.background_ko: 모듈 압축 파일을 검증하기 전에 해제하는 문제가 있다.

CVE-2026-3859.description: XSS vulnerability in Vibe Versions <= 4.0.8.7 could allow an attacker to inject malicious JavaScript through crafted search input.

CVE-2026-3860.description: CSRF vulnerability in OpenText Vibe versions <= 4.0.8.7 could expose the token over an insecure connection or make it accessible to JavaScript, weakening protection against forged requests.

CVE-2026-28731.description: A memory corruption vulnerability exists in VideoLAN VLC 3.0.23. A specially crafted Interplay MVE file can trigger a condition that allows access to a variable that is not explicitly initialized, which under certain conditions can lead to code execution in the context of the current process.
CVE-2026-28731.summary_ko: VideoLAN VLC 3.0.23에 메모리 손상 취약점이 있다. 조작된 Interplay MVE 파일을 처리하면 특정 조건에서 현재 프로세스 내 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있다.
CVE-2026-28731.background_ko: Interplay MVE 파일 처리 중 명시적으로 초기화되지 않은 변수에 접근할 수 있는 상태가 발생한다.

CVE-2026-32789.description: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in VideoLAN VLC 3.0.23. By using a specially crafted NUV file, an attacker could exploit this vulnerability to perform an out-of-bounds read, potentially leading to the disclosure of sensitive information.

CVE-2026-100101.description: On Linux and other Unix-like systems, LibreOffice can send the current document as an email attachment with File > Send > Email Document, which starts the mail client through a script bundled with LibreOffice. The script let the shell interpret the name of the document's file, so a file with a crafted name could run commands when it was sent by email. In fixed versions the script passes the file name and the other details to the mail client as plain arguments.
CVE-2026-100101.summary_ko: Linux 등 Unix 계열의 LibreOffice에서 문서를 이메일 첨부로 전송할 때 조작된 문서 파일명으로 인해 명령이 실행될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-100101.background_ko: 메일 클라이언트를 실행하는 LibreOffice 포함 스크립트가 문서 파일명을 셸이 해석하도록 처리했다.

CVE-2026-101351.description: LibreOffice can import PICT images, which may be embedded in documents. Parts of a crafted image could be left unwritten, so leftover memory became part of the imported image and could be saved with the document. In fixed versions the pixels of a new image start out cleared, so any part the image data does not fill is blank.

CVE-2026-101352.description: A document can carry its own user interface customizations, such as keyboard shortcuts, menus and toolbars, which take effect while the document is open. A command bound in these customizations could run a macro or a script even when the macro security settings did not allow the macros of the document, so a user who pressed a shortcut or chose a menu item in a crafted document could run code without any warning. In fixed versions the customizations of a document are treated like its other macro content, and the macro and script commands in them are only kept when the macros of the document are allowed.
CVE-2026-101352.summary_ko: 문서에 포함된 단축키나 메뉴 명령을 사용하면 매크로 보안 설정이 문서의 매크로를 금지하더라도 경고 없이 코드가 실행될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-101352.background_ko: 문서의 사용자 인터페이스 사용자 지정에 연결된 매크로·스크립트 명령에 문서의 매크로 보안 제한이 적용되지 않았다.

CVE-2026-101353.description: LibreOffice Base documents can contain an embedded HSQLDB database, and other documents can use such a database as a data source. The definition of the database in a crafted document could make the database engine create or write files at locations outside the document, chosen by the document. In fixed versions the files of an embedded database are kept in a private location, and an embedded database cannot create table files anywhere else.

CVE-2026-101892.description: LibreOffice documents in ODF format can contain form controls, such as buttons and text fields, and each control names the component that implements it. The component a control named was created even when it was not a form control, and the settings stored with the control were applied to it, so a crafted document could change the configuration of LibreOffice in a way that led to code being run. In fixed versions a control whose component is not a form control is ignored.
CVE-2026-101892.summary_ko: LibreOffice에서 조작된 ODF 문서의 양식 컨트롤을 통해 프로그램 설정이 변경되고 코드가 실행될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-101892.background_ko: 양식 컨트롤이 지정한 구성 요소가 실제 양식 컨트롤이 아니어도 생성하고, 컨트롤에 저장된 설정을 해당 구성 요소에 적용했다.

CVE-2026-101929.description: LibreOffice documents can contain Basic macro libraries. A library protected by a password is stored in the document in a compiled form, which may be read when the document is loaded. When a value in the compiled form used an older record format, it could be read as a different type from the one the existing value held, which corrupted memory. In fixed versions the existing value is cleared before a value in the older format is read.

CVE-2026-101930.description: LibreOffice Writer can open HTML documents, and an HTML document can bind macros to events of the document as a whole, such as the document being opened or closed. Macros bound to these events were not taken into account by the macro security check, so they could run when the document was opened, whatever the macro security level. In fixed versions these macros follow the macro security settings like any other macro in the document.
CVE-2026-101930.summary_ko: LibreOffice Writer에서 HTML 문서를 열면 문서 이벤트에 연결된 매크로가 매크로 보안 수준과 관계없이 실행될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-101930.background_ko: 매크로 보안 검사에서 HTML 문서 전체의 열기·닫기 이벤트에 연결된 매크로를 검사 대상에 포함하지 않았다.

CVE-2026-101933.description: LibreOffice documents can contain Basic macro libraries. A library protected by a password is stored in the document in a compiled form, which may be read when the document is loaded. An out-of-bounds write existed when the compiled form was read, because the positions of its strings were not checked against the size of the data they refer to, and a type found by name was not checked to be of the right kind. In fixed versions these positions are checked, a library that fails the check is not loaded, and a type of the wrong kind is ignored.

CVE-2026-104007.description: LibreOffice can connect to databases through JDBC drivers written in Java. A spreadsheet can use a database as the source of a pivot table, and the database document that describes the connection names the driver to use. The location the driver was loaded from was taken from the database document itself, so a crafted document could make LibreOffice load and run Java code that the document supplied when it was opened. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63277. In fixed versions the driver location is taken only from the driver configuration of the user, and a pivot table whose source is a database document named by a URL connects only once the user allows links to be updated.
CVE-2026-104007.summary_ko: LibreOffice의 피벗 테이블용 데이터베이스 연결에서 조작된 문서를 열면 문서가 제공한 Java 코드가 JDBC 드라이버로 로드·실행될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-104007.background_ko: JDBC 드라이버를 불러올 위치를 데이터베이스 문서 자체에서 가져왔다.

CVE-2026-104692.description: LibreOffice bundles the HSQLDB database engine, which can be used through the generic JDBC database driver as well as through the support for embedded databases. HSQLDB lets SQL statements call Java methods, limited to the classes that are permitted. When HSQLDB was used through the generic JDBC driver this limit did not apply, so SQL in a crafted document could call any Java method and run code. In fixed versions SQL can call only the built-in functions of HSQLDB, whichever way the database is reached.
CVE-2026-104692.summary_ko: LibreOffice에 포함된 HSQLDB를 일반 JDBC 드라이버로 사용할 때, 조작된 문서의 SQL이 임의의 Java 메서드를 호출해 코드를 실행할 수 있다.
CVE-2026-104692.background_ko: HSQLDB를 일반 JDBC 드라이버로 사용할 때 SQL에서 호출할 수 있는 Java 클래스 제한이 적용되지 않았다.

CVE-2026-104920.description: LibreOffice Calc can link a cell range to an external data source, and the link is saved in the document. A Java database driver for such a link is loaded from a class path. Opening a crafted document could still load a Java database driver from a location outside the local machine and run its code, by a route that the fix for CVE-2026-63277 did not cover. In fixed versions an entry in a Java class path has to be a file URL that names a file on the local machine.
CVE-2026-104920.summary_ko: LibreOffice Calc에서 외부 데이터 원본에 연결된 조작된 문서를 열면 로컬 컴퓨터 밖의 Java 데이터베이스 드라이버가 로드되고 해당 코드가 실행될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-104920.background_ko: Java 데이터베이스 드라이버의 클래스 경로에 로컬 컴퓨터 밖의 위치도 허용됐으며, 이 로드 경로는 기존 수정에 포함되지 않았다.
