According to its own timestamps, GPT-Live began to answer 800 ms after the end of the line, close to the 0.8 s published by OpenAI; most of the remaining wait, about 1,367 ms and nearly constant, is the audio's round trip through OpenAI's service. A tool call added 0.9-1.1 s in every architecture, more than any difference between them, and the frameworks' self-reported latency fell short of the listener's wait by 9% (Pipecat) and 22% (LiveKit). Word error rates were low (6.03, 4.93 and 1.47%), but the error on amounts was 13.01% and 12.61% in the cascades, against 2.86%

95656784877dfa70ac8f0b05.title_original: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
95656784877dfa70ac8f0b05.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achieved impressive results, current frameworks remain largely confined to ``flat" 2D controls (e.g., text prompts, bounding boxes, or masks). Precise 3D-aware geometric manipulation -- such as coordinating an object's location, physical scale, and 3D orientation while strictly preserving its fine-grained identity -- remains an elusive challenge, typically suffering from severe detail degradation or requiring expensive per-instance fine-tuning. In this paper, we present DecoEdit, an all-in-one image editing framework that goes beyond flat control by seamlessly integrating 1D textual, 2D spatial, and 3D volumetric inputs under a unified architecture. First, to power this unified model, we establish a data curation pipeline and curate a large-scale dataset, namely DecoDataset, containing 1.6 million samples, encompassing diverse multi-dimensional (1D/2D/3D) tasks and their complex compositions. Furthermore, we establish a comprehensive image editing benchmark named DecoBench to systematically evaluate multi-task editing performance. Finally, to address the fundamental trade-off between complex spatial transformations and identity preservation, we propose a novel decoupled pipeline: DecoEdit factorizes the editing process by utilizing structural guidance from SAM-3D to anchor the target geometry, scale, and spatial orientation, while concurrently leveraging a detail-preservat

37a8895c54e7bcd9ab75c826.title_original: Beyond Plain MCP: Do Decision Models and Code Mode Make Tool Use Cheaper and Faster?
37a8895c54e7bcd9ab75c826.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways manage tool catalogs for language model agents using two primary paradigms: code mode where agents write scripts against tool stubs and decision layers which are cheap routers that preselect tool subsets. Using a controlled harness across 12 servers, up to 1,958 distractor tools, and three open-weight agents including Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron, we present a preregistered evaluation on a sealed test split to determine when each approach succeeds. Code mode substantially outperforms plain MCP, cutting token usage by 70 to 90 percent while significantly boosting utility. Declaring return-shape hints in code mode stubs is a first-order variable, swinging success by up to 39.5 points for lower-performing agents, an effect larger than adding a router. The central hypothesis that a decision layer in front of code mode beats code mode alone is not confirmed, showing minor, statistically non-significant improvements for weaker agents and a slight cost for the strongest. We publicly release our harness, a finetuned 4B tool selection model, and all evaluation traces to support robust community experimentation on local AI privacy and agent architectures.

90aedef0485c7541ce29df87.title_original: How Much Determinism Can Fine-Tuning Buy? Margin Regularisation Against Batch-Induced Token Flips
90aedef0485c7541ce29df87.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Greedy decoding at zero temperature is widely assumed to be deterministic, although the exact same prompt may yield different tokens depending on the number of other prompts sharing the batch for inference. The currently available solutions operate during inference, trading determinism for throughput. Can we train a model in such a way that fewer decoding steps would be susceptible? We characterize the perturbation empirically across six model families and three numerical precisions and observe two empirical facts about the measurement: the perturbation depends exactly on the representable precision (8.00x for bfloat16 vs float16, 8192.0x for float16 vs float32, in line with predictions based on mantissa bits) and the batch invariance happens accidentally at certain tensor shapes, allowing a practitioner to achieve zero nondeterminism merely by setting the sequence length. Then we apply hinge penalization of the model's top-1 / top-2 logit gap, scaled to twice the measured noise quantile. On GSM8K dataset it leads to a 35% reduction in token flips and divergence from 53.8% to 38.1%, at the cost of 1.3 - 2.9 accuracy points, increasing monotonically with the margin size. It does not affect the gap threshold sufficient for determinism: the logit gaps of surviving flips are unchanged (median 0.125 for all arms), as the hinge is a soft penalty and the largest hardware perturbation remains the same. We reject seven hypotheses, incl

3e15dbf699eda2d74f08de63.title_original: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development
3e15dbf699eda2d74f08de63.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As agentic systems are increasingly deployed to support complex Web tasks, multi-agent architectures offer greater parallelism, specialization, and task coverage. However, increasing the number of agents does not necessarily improve system performance, as communication, synchronization, redundant work, and coordination overhead may offset the benefits of additional agents. This presents a fundamental scaling challenge for agentic Web systems: how can agent populations be organized to balance task performance and coordination costs? To address this challenge, we systematically investigate the relationship between agent population size, per-agent token consumption, and coordination overhead in collaborative agentic systems. Experiments on complex Web-oriented software development tasks reveal a non-linear scaling pattern: per-agent token consumption initially decreases as the agent population grows, but eventually exhibits diminishing returns. Motivated by these findings, we introduce the Surgical Team Model (STM), a structured coordination framework that organizes agents through role specialization, constrained inter-agent communication, and coordinator-mediated task aggregation. Experiments on full-stack Web application development tasks show that STM achieves competitive task completion quality and comparable token consumption relative to representative baselines, while incurring higher execution latency.

a6542a16c3eb1e2a0397fb63.title_original: MarineSparkLM-4B: A Lightweight Language Model for Marine and Offshore Engineering Built by Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
a6542a16c3eb1e2a0397fb63.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Marine and offshore engineering text is spread across preprints, open-access journals, encyclopedias and institutional documents, and the amount of it is small by pretraining standards. We ask how far a lightweight language model for marine and offshore engineering can be taken with parameter-efficient adaptation on a single workstation-class device. Starting from the 4-billion-parameter OceanGPT-basic-4B-Instruct, we train two independent LoRA adapters, each updating 33.0 million of 4.06 billion parameters (0.81%). Training took 4 hours 40 minutes for the first adapter and 10 minutes for the second on one NVIDIA DGX Spark. The first adapter is trained by next-token prediction on a 61.6-million-token corpus covering ten engineering themes. The corpus was built from 13,879 source documents, of which 7,069 were retained after deduplication and a two-tier keyword filter that removes cross-domain lexical collisions. Its validation loss falls from 2.082 to 1.976 over 1,500 steps. Direct testing showed that this adapter could still drift off topic on a retrieval-grounded ballast-water prompt, so we trained a second adapter on 2,295 question-answer pairs (114 hand-written and 2,181 generated by the base model from corpus passages) with the loss restricted to answer tokens. On 20 held-out prompts scored by hand for accuracy, topicality and specificity (maximum 120), the plain base model, the continuation adapter, the instruction adapt

ab00b19da1a8967cd9597d40.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19163v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schr\"odinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

b9305e3f0dd595419c22f267.title_original: Isolating Perception for Multi-View Planning under Occlusion-Induced Partial Observability
b9305e3f0dd595419c22f267.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are beginning to saturate visual planning benchmarks, yet they fail to resolve depth ambiguity and degrade sharply with problem size under occlusion-induced partial observability (PO). We introduce BW-PO based on the Blocksworld domain, a controlled benchmark that reduces existing VLM planners and formalizers to near-zero performance, and propose VLM-as-perceiver, a paradigm that narrows the VLM's role to local perception while delegating cross-view evidence reconciliation and plan generation to external solvers. Across model-specific challenging subsets of BW-PO, this raises plan success from 1% to 97% for Gemma-4-31B, 0% to 95% for Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 3% to 84% for Gemini-3.1-Pro. Isolating perception in this way separates two bottlenecks that are otherwise entangled: reconciliation under depth ambiguity, and completeness of visual extraction under scene density.

ccd8f6485a9e5274f521bce0.title_original: On-policy distillation as a Backdoor Propagation Channel
ccd8f6485a9e5274f521bce0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for the post training of large language models, improving student models by leveraging supervision generated online by teacher models. However, whether this process also transfers latent security risks from teacher models to student models remains insufficiently studied. In this work, we reveal a new security risk in which an attacker first implants a conditional backdoor into the teacher model through supervised fine tuning (SFT), after which OPD can transfer the backdoor to the student model with only an extremely small proportion of trigger prompt exposure. More concerningly, we find that such backdoor transfer is substantially stronger under OPD than under conventional distillation methods, suggesting that OPD may provide an efficient channel for propagating backdoors across models. Our mechanistic analysis shows that the backdoor signal is primarily transmitted through anomalous differences in the conditional probabilities produced by the teacher model for triggered and clean inputs, and is gradually internalized into the internal representations of the student model during training. Furthermore, we investigate how to suppress such anomalous conditional probability signals at the source of distillation supervision and, based on this analysis, propose an OPD training method tailored to this conditional backdoor propagation setting to mitigate the risk of bac
ccd8f6485a9e5274f521bce0.title_ko: 온폴리시 증류가 교사 모델의 백도어를 학생 모델로 전파할 수 있다는 연구
ccd8f6485a9e5274f521bce0.summary_ko: 연구진은 지도 미세조정으로 교사 모델에 심은 조건부 백도어가 온폴리시 증류(OPD)를 통해 학생 모델로 전파될 수 있다고 보고했다. 극소량의 트리거 프롬프트 노출만으로 전이가 발생했고, 기존 증류 방식보다 강하게 나타났다는 설명이다. 트리거 입력에 대한 교사 모델의 비정상적 조건부 확률 차이를 전파 경로로 분석하고, 이를 억제하는 학습 방법을 제안했다.
ccd8f6485a9e5274f521bce0.background_ko: 교사 모델이 온라인으로 생성한 지도 신호를 활용하는 OPD가 확산되는 가운데, 잠재적 보안 위험도 학생 모델에 전달되는지는 충분히 연구되지 않았다.

curation.reason_ko: 온라인 증류가 교사 모델의 조건부 백도어를 학생에게 전달할 수 있다는 실험이 모델 학습 공급망 위험을 제기했다.

394e921428cd1e5f684f7898.title_original: Neural Dual Bounds: Valid-by-Construction JGLP Warm-Starts for MAP and Constrained MAP
394e921428cd1e5f684f7898.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Neural Dual Bounds, a calibration-free framework that produces deterministic upper bounds for MAP inference in probabilistic graphical models using a single neural-network forward pass. The framework trains a network to output the edge messages of a mini-bucket style upper bound on a given join-graph decomposition in a self-supervised manner by directly minimizing a smooth dual objective. The output of this network can be used at test time to warm-start a standard JGLP optimizer. Across diverse benchmarks, this warm start yields dual gaps that are orders of magnitude tighter than those from zero initialization, with the largest gains in the early-iteration regime. We also apply our framework for the constrained MAP (CMPE) task, where neural warm starts with test-time adaptation are comparable to the adaptive baseline on Bayesian networks and achieve the tightest dual gaps, by one to two orders of magnitude, on the grid and segmentation families.

0c1138f9ed6584bf56857899.title_original: Revisiting What Makes a Good Context Subset: A Sparse Latent Basis Perspective
0c1138f9ed6584bf56857899.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Selecting context subsets is increasingly important in modern LLM inference, yet what makes a subset effective remains unclear. We study this question in the controlled setting of few-shot demonstration selection. We examine a hypothesis that demonstrations should collectively provide task-relevant information needed by a target query. Assuming that the query representation provides a useful proxy for these requirements, we formulate selection as sparse reconstruction and instantiate it with Residual Explanation Search (RES), a Matching-Pursuit-style diagnostic procedure. Across seven benchmarks and eight open-weight LLMs, no retrieval objective is universally best. RES outperforms MMR in 34 of 56 model--dataset pairs, with its clearest advantage on sentiment tasks, suggesting that query-conditioned collective reconstruction may capture useful complementarity that pairwise dissimilarity misses. Relevance-based retrieval remains strong on template-heavy reasoning benchmarks, while all retrieval methods underperform zero-shot prediction on average on StrategyQA, where a solution-reconstruction analysis is consistent with the query not exposing the required external knowledge. Target-model hidden states further show that retrieval objectives interact differently with representation spaces: middle-layer representations generally favor similarity retrieval, whereas last-layer representations are often stronger for residual- and div

5de98a40e5cc302fffe6c61d.title_original: Beyond Alignment: Supervising the Generator for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction
5de98a40e5cc302fffe6c61d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual brain decoding translates neural activity into human-interpretable images. While recent EEG-to-image reconstruction methods rely on aligning EEG signals with pretrained visual embeddings to condition an image generator, we empirically demonstrate that stronger cross-modal alignment do not translate into comparable gains in reconstruction quality. This indicates that improving the input condition alone is insufficient; the generative process itself requires explicit supervision. Although Representation Alignment (REPA) offers a solution by guiding diffusion transformers with pretrained vision encoder features, we find that EEG-conditioned generators struggle to follow these fixed targets. To address this mismatch, we introduce generation-derived supervision (GDS): an image-conditioned teacher that translates static image-encoder features into the internal representation space of a diffusion transformer. Our EEG-conditioned student generator closely tracks these dynamic targets during denoising, discarding the teacher at inference. Evaluated on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG, our approach consistently outperforms conditioning-centric baselines, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity.

6dc895e4c4befbe8ec229095.title_original: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
6dc895e4c4befbe8ec229095.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks fail in ways that end-task success cannot see. HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, each two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation: the state one step leaves (an object pose, a choice, a fact seen once) determines what the next step must do, unlike benchmarks that place sub-tasks side by side. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check of a chore. From each trajectory the benchmark reads where a chain breaks, what the agent did after a failed call, and how far its own position estimate drifts from the true one. This version reports first results only: 15 of 60 planned runs (three models at high effort, one run each on chores T1 and T10 from both start states and T3 from one), with scripted-robot proofs on three of the ten chores. Of the 15 runs, 2 passed all five sub-tasks. Runs still going after sub-tasks 1 to 5 were 15, 8, 4, 2, 2. Of 189 failed calls, 168 were followed by a different call and 111 by a call that did not fail. These are first results and not a full benchmark. We will release the scenes, task chains, scripted robot, evaluation harness and trajectories.

90f78f6fb9e3762e40791509.title_original: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
90f78f6fb9e3762e40791509.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SAR-to-optical translators often synthesize detail that the radar measurement does not support, and pixel metrics alone cannot reveal it. We propose SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for frozen generators: a stochastic sampler draws K candidates (Monte Carlo dropout for GANs, seed variance for diffusion), a speckle-aware verifier ranks them by gradient-magnitude correlation with the SAR input and a hallucination-frequency index, and a SAR-guided frequency gate admits high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it. With all five hyperparameters frozen and three training seeds, we evaluate on 500 scene-disjoint SEN1-2 test patches, 500 patches of a held-out summer scene, and 200 cross-dataset SEN12MS winter pairs. The layer improves Pix2Pix by +0.060, +0.012, and +0.077 dB PSNR and by +0.0034, +0.0057, and +0.0135 SSIM, respectively (Wilcoxon p < 1e-6), and it improves CycleGAN and CUT on all three sets (+0.013 to +0.076 dB). It raises edge precision at the cost of edge recall (edge F1 -1.3% on the test set). On the latent diffusion model COP-GEN, it adds +0.33 dB (base) and +0.16 dB (Beta) on the winter set, the only set with dual-polarization SAR. An ablation shows that the gate produces the gain for MC-dropout GANs, whose candidates are nearly identical, whereas verifier selection contributes up to +0.26 dB for diffusion, whose samples differ. The layer has zero trainable parameters and adds 0.4 ms pe

5678ae76ba442f16070f3a6c.title_original: Generation of protein conformations using a simple inverted transformer
5678ae76ba442f16070f3a6c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular dynamics is an extremely powerful approach for studying protein behavior, but it requires enormous computational resources to obtain an adequate sampling of possible conformations. Recently, thanks to successes in predicting three-dimensional protein structures, there has been an explosion of research exploring the opportunities offered by deep learning to address the problem of protein conformational landscape. In this work, an artificial intelligence system based on a variant of the Transformer architecture is introduced and applied to the problem of determining the ensemble of three-dimensional structures that a protein can access and their statistical weight. After being trained on a dataset of conformations of a particular protein obtained using classical all-atom molecular dynamics, this neural network is able to directly generate physically plausible protein conformations similar to those obtained both through molecular dynamics and experimentally. The ordered sequence of conformations obtained as output of the neural network rapidly converges towards the most populated regions of the protein's conformational landscape, suggesting that the system may have learned not only the protein's three-dimensional organization but also the thermodynamic weights of the various feasible conformations. These features, combined with its simplicity and low computational load, make this Transformer variant an ideal candidate f

af19fe85717edf2570bd19c5.title_original: Benchmarking the State of AI for Crop Yield Forecasting: A Global Assessment Across Modeling Paradigms
af19fe85717edf2570bd19c5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate crop yield forecasting is essential for food security, agricultural policy, and commodity markets. Although statistical, process-based, and machine learning approaches have all been proposed, their relative strengths remain poorly understood due to the lack of large-scale, standardized comparisons. We address this gap through a comprehensive benchmark of five modeling paradigms -- statistical baselines, process-based models, conventional feature-engineered machine learning, deep sequence models, and tabular foundation models -- using the CY-Bench benchmark spanning 63 country-crop datasets (>12,000 administrative regions) across six continents. Beyond conventional pooled accuracy metrics, we introduce a multi-dimensional evaluation framework that separately quantifies overall, spatial, temporal, and anomaly prediction skill. Across multiple crops and countries, feature-engineered machine learning and tabular foundation models achieve the strongest overall predictive performance. Data-driven models reduce NRMSE in 72% of countries growing maize and 78% of countries growing wheat, with median reductions of 8.8% and 11.9%, respectively. Across all modeling paradigms, spatial prediction is substantially easier than temporal and anomaly prediction. While data-driven models markedly improve temporal and anomaly prediction over statistical baselines, accurately forecasting year-to-year yield variability remains challenging.

bb97eac1e4e912d290c6b4cd.title_original: OmitEHR: Scalable Omission Detection in LLM-Generated Clinical Summaries
bb97eac1e4e912d290c6b4cd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Health systems increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to draft summaries of patient medical records, yet evaluations now find omissions, the absence of clinically important information, to be the most common failure mode. Detecting omissions in an LLM-generated summary requires knowing which facts in the record are salient, a signal that existing methods hand-specify, ignore, or recompute at inference with costly LLM judges. We present OmitEHR, a reference-free omission detector that learns clinical salience from historical clinician-written summaries predating widespread LLM use. OmitEHR learns to predict which source-note sentences clinicians include in their summaries, then surfaces high-salience sentences not covered by an LLM-generated summary as candidate omissions. We apply OmitEHR to brief hospital course (BHC) summarization using 5,000 admissions from a large academic medical center. On held-out admissions, OmitEHR outperformed all evaluated baselines at predicting salient source sentences, including a prompted LLM judge. The full omission detection pipeline took 17.7 to 19.5 seconds and cost \$0.03 to \$0.13 per summary depending on the base model, 1.6 to 1.7 times faster and 5.6 to 6.7 times cheaper than scoring every source sentence with an LLM judge. In a blinded review of 25 admissions, two board-certified clinicians confirmed a mean of 5.6 clinically meaningful omissions per summary surfaced by OmitEH

101cd3425222392d06dc3fb6.title_original: SMELL: Sparsity-aware Memory Efficient Federated Fine-tuning for Long-context LLMs
101cd3425222392d06dc3fb6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19349v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated fine-tuning enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to collaboratively adapt to distributed private data. However, long-context fine-tuning on resource-constrained devices faces substantial challenges arising from excessive activation memory, heterogeneous token-importance patterns across clients, and communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose SMELL, a Sparsity-aware and Memory-Efficient federated fine-tuning framework for Long-context LLMs. SMELL integrates three complementary mechanisms: Local Sparse-Forward Adaptation (LSFA), Consensus-Anchored Sparsity Coordination (CASC), and Communication-Efficient Progressive Update Recovery (CPUR). These mechanisms jointly enable memory-efficient local adaptation, heterogeneity-aware sparsity coordination, and lightweight model-update transmission. Experiments on OPT-350M and LLaMA2-7B demonstrate that SMELL reduces peak memory consumption by up to 88.35% compared with conventional fine-tuning and 13.25% compared with forward-only LoRA fine-tuning at a 16K context length. Furthermore, SMELL improves fine-tuning performance under certain non-IID settings and supports compact update transmission with progressive reconstruction, demonstrating its potential for resource-efficient federated long-context LLM adaptation.

b6473ea14e1a3945cf9d8b5f.title_original: Pixel-KWS: Rendered-Glyph Representations for Orthographically Robust Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting
b6473ea14e1a3945cf9d8b5f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting (KWS) allows users to enroll arbitrary keywords at inference time. However, character and phoneme-based text encoders rely on fixed symbol vocabularies learned during training, limiting their ability to handle unseen or visually similar symbols such as homoglyphs, l33tspeak substitutions, and accented characters. We propose PIXEL-KWS, an open-vocabulary KWS framework that represents characters through rendered glyphs rather than learned embedding lookups. We render each character as a grayscale image and encode it with a lightweight CNN, enabling the text encoder to generalize from visual form rather than a fixed vocabulary. On LibriPhrase, PIXEL-KWS and its matched character-based counterpart achieve 9.57% and 9.55% EER on LibriPhrase-hard, 0.43% and 0.41% EER on LibriPhrase-easy, outperforming all published baselines without pre-training or synthetic data. PIXEL-KWS provides substantially greater robustness to both homoglyph and l33tspeak symbol-level perturbations. These results highlight glyph-based representations as a simple and effective approach for robust open-vocabulary KWS in practical settings.

4e2a4295082d22bf7e553d29.title_original: Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?
4e2a4295082d22bf7e553d29.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Matrix-structured optimizers can improve language-model pretraining, but it is unclear whether these gains transfer to short-horizon KL distillation from an instruction-tuned initialization. We compare AdamW and diagonal AdaGrad with two tractable Shampoo reductions, SOAP, and All-2D Muon across four dense Qwen student-teacher pairs under a common forward-KL objective and fixed training budget. Across scales, none of the evaluated matrix-structured recipes consistently improves the quality versus trainer-time trade-off over the elementwise references: AdamW generally attains the lowest validation KL, while AdaGrad can be slightly faster at larger scale. SOAP often tracks AdamW in KL but incurs substantial trainer-time overhead, and the two Shampoo reductions reverse ordering across model pairs, showing that conclusions depend on the feasible recipe. These results suggest that pretraining optimizer gains do not transfer automatically to KL distillation and should be re-established for the target objective and systems regime.

1421039666a55a020376d909.title_original: Prepare Lighter and Faster for Open-Vocabulary Queries: A Query-Wise 3D Segmenter for Gaussian Splatting
1421039666a55a020376d909.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D understanding aims to localize and segment arbitrary objects beyond predefined categories. However, existing approaches based on Gaussian Splatting often rely on expensive preprocessing and lengthy training, limiting their applicability when fast and lightweight solutions are desired. We propose a lightweight, training-free framework for query-driven 3D instance segmentation on Gaussian Splatting. Instead of conventional mask-wise CLIP embeddings, we use dense pixel-level CLIP features to preserve fine-grained semantic information and enable flexible text-driven localization without relying on predefined instance proposals. Given a text query, we identify a high-quality target region in a carefully selected pivot view and propagate it across views using a video segmentor, providing consistent and comprehensive coverage of the target instance. We then lift the resulting 2D tracklets to 3D Gaussians through a novel visibility voting strategy, yielding accurate 3D segmentation masks with clean object boundaries. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on LERF-OVS, ScanNet, and ScanNet++, competitive results on 3D-OVS, and significant speedups over existing open-vocabulary 3D segmentation methods. These results highlight the effectiveness of our framework for efficient open-vocabulary 3D understanding without per-scene training.

8ca7f0ded859432b9ea6a941.title_original: Do Rule-Based Tools Help LLMs Translate Endangered Uralic Languages in the Prompt or over MCP?
8ca7f0ded859432b9ea6a941.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Komi-Zyrian, Moksha, Erzya and Udmurt have mature rule-based resources, among them finite-state analysers, constraint grammars and bilingual dictionaries, which language models do not use. We ask whether giving a model access to these resources improves machine translation from the four languages into English, and whether it matters how the access is provided: as analyses computed in advance and written into the prompt, or as tools that the model calls itself through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We evaluate manually: an expert linguist read every English output of the strongest model under three conditions, 816 sentences in all, accepted or rejected each one, and named the main error in every rejected translation. With the analyses in the prompt, the number of accepted translations rises from 13 to 43 out of 272; with the tools attached it rises to 55. The gain comes from the bilingual dictionary. For Udmurt, whose dictionary has no English side, the prompt-based condition brings no gain at all, while for the other three languages an English gloss reaches the prompt for 74 to 80% of the source words. Tool calling is also much harder to get working than prompt injection. Of 31 open-weight models, 14 never call a tool, 11 of them because they cannot produce a usable call, and half of the calls that are made name a language the toolkit does not support. We release the data set, every model output and all tool-call logs.

f35861a9793dd455ccb458ab.title_original: CLEW: Log-Anchored Backward Tracing for Root-Cause Code Localization
f35861a9793dd455ccb458ab.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19448v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Failures in industrial software systems may involve multiple components and be difficult to reproduce outside the production environment. Root-cause code localization therefore often relies on issue descriptions and runtime logs. However, log evidence may be noisy or incomplete, and the code reporting a symptom may differ from the code containing the underlying defect. These conditions make it challenging to identify relevant log evidence and determine which functions could have caused the reported failure. To address this gap, we introduce CLEW, an agentic approach that combines rule-based log-to-code anchoring with LLM-guided backward code tracing. CLEW organizes selected observations into diagnostic states, guides source exploration from anchored symptom functions, and returns ranked candidate functions, an affected module, and an explanation comprising a proposed mechanism path and associated log events. For evaluation, we construct LogLoc, a benchmark comprising 192 real-world issue and fault-injection cases. Against three baselines, CLEW records the highest observed Acc@1 (77.3%) and MRR (81.3%) on LogLoc-Issues and matches the leading baselines at 97.6% Acc@1 on LogLoc-Airflow. Averaged over all 192 cases, CLEW's wall-clock time is approximately 73% lower than LocAgent's at a similar average inference cost. No aggregate degradation is observed under the tested perturbations, with modest changes in Acc@1 and MRR across t

b788856359a2682e6f613bcb.title_original: VAST: Compiling Grounded Vulnerability Scenarios into Verifiable, Multi-Step Environments for Evaluating LLM Red-Team Agents
b788856359a2682e6f613bcb.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) security agents requires reproducible environments whose workflow difficulty can be varied and whose failures can be diagnosed. We present VAST (Verifiable Adversarial Scenario Training & Evaluation), a declarative range compiler separating vulnerability scenarios from a compiler-introduced workflow-hardening layer. Following a post-hoc code and AST audit across all topics, the main benchmark retains 109 seed edges (45 with strict upstream CVE annotations), 72 family identifiers (62 under shared-HMAC relay grouping), 81 topic configurations (76 core plus 5 bounded execution models), and 1,387 instances (359 canonical four-gate-revalidated specs plus 1,028 seed variants) in a 42:39 partition. On the TopicServer compiler stratum, a budget-matched 270-episode prompt contrast across 10 compiled mechanism-family clusters (30 P2/P3/P4 instances, 40 turns, temperature 0.0) shows that glm-5.3, grok-4.7, and deepseek-v4-pro solve 12/90 instances under contract_only and 14/90 under generic_hint (cluster sign p=1.00), whereas supplying the shared workflow protocol in full_guide lifts completion to 76/90 (28/30, 23/30, 25/30; cluster sign p<=0.00391). On the separate ranges_v2 ledger, a 126-episode evaluation across 6 non-TopicServer workflows and multi-container Docker/Linux stacks solves 88/126 (69.8%) (28/42, 31/42, 29/42), while an 18-episode intervention on asynchronous Redis worker chaining (v2_

5234a2acdf5af5ae37bbe6c8.title_original: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
5234a2acdf5af5ae37bbe6c8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. The alignment term is provably invariant to the rank means, so it gives no incentive to collapse the ordinal axis. On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), a source-trained teacher reaches 1.6 to 1.9 days mean absolute error (MAE) on the other species, with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) below zero. The 423K-parameter student, 2.54 times smaller than its teacher, attains the lowest MAE (1.476 days) and highest within 1-day accuracy (56.1%) among 14 configurations, matching the best of six ImageNet-pretrained backbones (ConvNeXt-T, 1.503 days) at 66 times fewer parameters, 1.44ms per cube on a GPU and 5s re-adaptation. InvarOrd beats target-only training by 0.29 days (p = 0.031). Among alignment objectives, rank-invariant alignment retains the most ordinal structure (embedding rank correlation 0.183, QWK 0.112), whereas global discrepancy lowers the rank correlation to 0.049 and QWK to zero at only 0.0

c13ca4f8666b6d9a8c77bc86.title_original: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
c13ca4f8666b6d9a8c77bc86.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from a covariance-adjusted discriminant to the mean difference, and evaluate probing and additive steering, which adds the direction to the hidden state, along the family at a fixed side effect. For truthfulness and sentiment, in every model, the best probe is not the best steering direction: steering consistently favors directions closer to the mean difference. This separation holds across 59 of 60 layer-model-concept combinations in a layer sweep, with matched probe and steering texts in all six model-concept combinations, and under a rotation-based steering operator. The exact steering optimum is less stable: for sentiment, an intermediate direction produces a 27-56% stronger steering effect than the mean difference, but this gain shrinks or disappears with matched texts and depends on the layer and the operator. The two roles also transfer differently across models. A probe transferred by a linear map fitted on neutral text retains 81-91% of the target model's above-chance probing performance, while the transferred m

5eaa73dbd4c37d1d49c08d4c.title_original: Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents
5eaa73dbd4c37d1d49c08d4c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding agents now push code, publish packages, call model APIs and operate cloud resources on behalf of developers. They authenticate to these services with the same bearer secrets humans use, personal access tokens, API keys and package-registry tokens, stored where the model, its subprocesses and any co-resident malware can read them. Incidents in 2025 and 2026, including prompt-injection attacks on coding agents and self-propagating supply-chain worms, show that this arrangement fails in predictable ways. Passkeys solved the analogous problem for humans, but they require a human gesture on every use and cannot be operated by an autonomous process. We present the Agent Authenticator, a design that gives agents passkey-grade authentication properties: per-service hardware-bound keys, no shared secrets, origin binding enforced by the runtime rather than the model, normalized attestation of the execution environment, human-signed scoped mandates, and cross-device human approval for high-risk actions. The same protocol serves agents on developer laptops and in cloud enclaves, and it deploys as a profile over existing mechanisms, MCP authorization, OAuth token exchange including the Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant, git and SSH, rather than as a new identity system. The authenticator also produces a signed, hash-chained record of each action it authorizes. We analyze the design against a threat model centered on prom

e88c110db1476ca092a4eaa6.title_original: Func-JEPA: Learning a Sobolev Space of Functions as Latent Vectors
e88c110db1476ca092a4eaa6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretraining an encoder once and reusing it across tasks is a widespread approach in vision and language. However, neural symbolic mathematics still trains a dedicated sequence-to-sequence model for each task, so that no representation of a function is shared. In this work, we propose the Function Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Func-JEPA, abbreviated f-JEPA): an encoder of mathematical functions, pretrained on their symbolic form, whose latent space imitates the Sobolev space H^1 and in which differentiation is a learned latent operator. The norm of a latent is computed exactly from the function, whereas its direction is learned to match Sobolev angles. The frozen encoder is then reused by lightweight modules for decoding, composition, integration, and regression from samples. The representation and four downstream tasks are evaluated within and outside the pretraining distribution. f-JEPA recovers exact formulas from noisy samples more often than the compared symbolic-regression methods, whereas computer algebra and task-specific models remain stronger on standard integration and differential-equation benchmarks.

becd554304ef3c7b13f5d72d.title_original: Beyond Prompts: Runtime Contracts for Coding Agents
becd554304ef3c7b13f5d72d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents act on repositories through shell commands and file edits, and teams steer them with written engineering rules. Industrial settings expect such rules to be enforced and their application to be evidenced, and a rule given as prompt text provides neither. We test whether executable contracts enforced while the agent works reduce rule violations compared with the same rules in the prompt, retrieved as guidance, or checked only after generation. Violations are scored by an oracle whose methods differ from the in-loop checks, and the oracle is validated by two human reviewers and a model reviewer. Across three studies on two model families (240, 112 and 108 runs), enforcement during execution produced no oracle-detected violation in 104 paired runs, against 21 to 55% of runs without rules, and no loss of functional correctness in the two confirmatory studies. In the confirmatory study on tasks aimed at known failure situations (Study 3, protocol hashed before the first run), enforcement lowered the share of violating runs by 31 percentage points relative to no rules (Holm-adjusted p = 0.014); the 17-point difference from prompted rules was not significant (p = 0.12), and neither was any contrast in Study 2, where only 3 of 14 tasks produced a violation. becd554304ef3c7b13f5d72d.title_ko: 코딩 에이전트 규칙 준수, 실행 중 계약 강제 방식으로 평가

d98da9739af3e1cd37079e16.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc explanations of deep-learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are difficult to trust because different attribution methods highlight different retinal regions for the same image, and a visually plausible heatmap does not show that the highlighted pixels drive the prediction. 24df71639af9b448ae4b76be.title_original: Inquest: Log-Guided Root-Cause Code Localization with a Staged Agent
24df71639af9b448ae4b76be.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a production issue is reported, engineers get a description and some logs, but no failing test and no way to reproduce the fault. The logs show where the failure was noticed, not where it was caused: in 49% of the real reports we study, the text names none of the files that the fix later changed. We built a benchmark for this setting from two public datasets and 27 open-source projects (Apache, Red Hat, MongoDB, MariaDB, Qt and Sakai). It holds 38,001 resolved issue reports with their pasted logs, the code as it was while the bug was still present, and the files the fix changed. We present INQUEST, an agent that finds the faulty code using a 27B open-weights model. Code, not the model, controls the procedure. It first gathers the evidence, including the files fixed in similar past issues that were resolved before the report was filed. The model then makes only three bounded decisions: which files to open, what role each file plays in the failure, and how to rank them. On 26,544 evaluation reports, INQUEST ranks a changed file first for 68.6% and in the top five for 85.9%, names the correct module for 90.2%, and ranks a changed function first for 53.8%. On the reports that name no faulty file, it reaches 52.8% and 73.6%. A free agent loop with the same model and tools finds files equally well, but names the faulty function 14 points less often. On a 1,000-report sample, INQUEST beats our reimplementations of two published

e02a269276bb615d59ef3e54.title_original: SemMask: Semantic-Prioritized Progressive Masking for Diffusion Language Models
e02a269276bb615d59ef3e54.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) are designed to enable globally parallel generation. However, in practice, they often exhibit pseudo-autoregressive behavior and a function-word-first bias, which undermines their performance on tasks such as text writing and code generation that benefit from global planning and parallel decoding. To address this, we propose SemMask, a novel fine-tuning paradigm that leverages a semantic-prioritized progressive masking strategy to encourage the model to decode high-information semantic tokens early and globally, thereby enhancing its global planning and parallel generation capabilities. Specifically, we first use the gradients of the original DLM with respect to each token to identify semantic tokens. During masking, these semantic tokens are preserved with priority, establishing a progressive generation order in which semantic tokens are decoded prior to function tokens. Meanwhile, we adjust the loss weight for semantic tokens to further reinforce their early prediction. Experimental results show that SemMask achieves quality comparable to strong autoregressive baselines on both text writing and code generation tasks, while providing superior semantic coherence. Notably, SemMask achieves higher accuracy with substantially fewer decoding steps, indicating that the early establishment of semantic structure improves the efficiency--accuracy trade-off.

cd0e3f4ca452c75570010be8.title_original: Read, Then Shade? How Visual Evidence Changes Incentive-Driven Misreporting in Vision-Language Advisors
cd0e3f4ca452c75570010be8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly read a scene and report it to someone who acts on the report, sometimes under objectives that differ from that person's. We ask whether a stated incentive moves what a VLM reports, and whether this changes when the value must be read from pixels rather than given as text. In seeded synthetic scenes, a model reads the position of a target on a labelled axis and reports one integer to a fixed receiver; it is paid, in simulation, for accuracy or for a report a few units to one side, and every scene is also presented with the true value as text. Across a pilot and three follow-up studies with hash-frozen protocols, four small open VLMs from three families, and 15,170 held-out trials, a stated payoff moved reports in both modalities, and exact compliance at three units was significantly lower with the image than with text for three of four models; Qwen2.5-VL 7B showed no reliable difference. Adding the true value as text to the image prompt removed the gap in every model. For InternVL3 the gap vanished on scenes it read correctly when it wrote its reading first; for Gemma 3 it persisted. For Qwen2.5-VL 3B, which read every scene correctly, the gap held in four of five payoff paraphrases, nearly vanished when the model wrote its reading before its report or when the prompt stated that the client wants the truth, vanished with an unpaid goal, and persisted when the model reported before stat

11dbbc436f13b4ba3696afc3.title_original: Learning from Mutants: Teaching Small Language Models to Synthesise Loop Invariants
11dbbc436f13b4ba3696afc3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19569v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have proven promising for synthesising loop invariants, a long-standing obstacle to automated program verification. Yet, frontier LLMs are typically accessible only through third-party APIs, hampering reproducibility and local deployment. Small language models (SLMs) sidestep these obstacles but require task-specific fine-tuning, for which high-quality training data is needed. We present a failure-driven data curation method for fine-tuning language models to synthesise loop invariants. Inspired by mutation testing, our approach applies semantic mutation operators to ground-truth invariants, producing semantic mutants that induce verification failure. Each mutant is paired with verifier feedback and its ground-truth counterpart, yielding training examples for feedback-guided invariant refinement. Whereas the vast space of mutants is a long-standing burden in mutation testing, it becomes an asset when generating training data, multiplying the examples obtainable from a fixed set of verified programs. We implement our approach for Dafny, augmenting an existing synthetic dataset of verified programs, and introduce a framework that iteratively refines candidate invariants using verifier feedback. On 472 DafnyBench programs, our best-performing fine-tuned Gemma-4-E4B configuration verifies 50.8% of programs zero-shot, compared to 8.1% for the base model, a 6.3$\times$ improvement. Higher-order mutants p

2f19dde5e1d5b5e43769811d.title_original: Spectral Steering: Local Inverse Geometry for Frozen Diffusion Generators
2f19dde5e1d5b5e43769811d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen diffusion generator may need to change several output properties while preserving others. We study when guidance faithfully realizes such a structured request and whether local inverse correction improves its direction. Our account links this benefit to the interaction between the request and the objective-specific remaining-sampler Jacobian: conditioning alone is insufficient. Spectral steering combines a request-specific cosine-gain predictor with damped inverse correction and fixed-time relinearization for finite edits. Scalar nulls and matched-movement controls test the predicted mechanism. Across 8,923 instances in a retrospectively identified local regime, predicted and realized gains correlate at Spearman 0.79, versus -0.11 for condition number. Experiments span images, audio, robotics, and control and planning, including complex character motion generation. On 50 paired inpainting cases, four corrections improve unobserved-pixel PSNR over Adam by 3.25 dB at equal total derivative traversals. Together, the analysis and controls connect request-dependent geometry to directional gains and establish where these gains translate into downstream performance.

49a73fd44e417664f9f5f2c2.title_original: Risk-Averse Decision-Focused Learning: Minimizing CVaR of Regret
49a73fd44e417664f9f5f2c2.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many combinatorial optimization (CO) problems involve parameters that are uncertain when the problem must be solved. In such settings, the parameters have to be predicted from correlated contextual information before a solution can be computed. \emph{Decision-focused learning} (DFL) addresses this by training the predictive model to produce predictions that optimize downstream decision quality. Most existing DFL methods are risk-neutral and minimize the expected regret. In high-stakes applications this can lead to undesirable outcomes, because decision-makers must also account for the tail risk of decision quality. Prior risk-sensitive approaches typically model uncertainty explicitly and solve a stochastic or robust optimization problem at inference time, which increases computational complexity. We instead propose a DFL framework that achieves risk-sensitive behavior while retaining point predictions and deterministic optimization at inference time. Starting from the dual representation of the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) and adding entropy regularization, we derive a smooth surrogate for the CVaR of regret. Its gradient induces an instance-dependent reweighting within each minibatch that emphasizes high-risk outcomes, so the approach can turn existing surrogate-loss DFL methods, including the SPO+ loss, into risk-sensitive variants. When instantiated with SPO+, the resulting objective admits a generalization bound on th

07cb6c428218a93529b18eb4.title_original: PBit1: One Programmable P-Bit per Parameter - A Finite-Control Representation of Pretrained Networks
07cb6c428218a93529b18eb4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce PBit1, a finite-control representation of pretrained neural networks that assigns one programmable p-bit to each learned parameter. A 12-bit command sets its probability, a shared affine range maps that probability to the weight domain, and temporal observations reconstruct the weight for inference. Operator-aware range grouping and sensitivity-based sampling allocation adapt the representation to the network. Across five independent weight draws at 32,768 observations per scalar, selected configurations preserve task quality in GPT-2, DistilBERT, and LFM3-1.7B with every learned scalar converted and no fine-tuning. GPT-2 and LFM3 perplexity increase by approximately 0.66% and 0.26%, respectively, while DistilBERT accuracy changes from 87.51% to 87.49%. A sensitivity-based policy reduces GPT-2 reconstruction observations by 41.7% while retaining the quality criterion. Complete-model evaluations reuse reconstructed weights in BF16 inference, and THRML operator experiments examine native sampling and spatial-temporal tradeoffs. Together, these results establish PBit1 as a concrete construction for studying finite-control weight representation and temporal reconstruction in pretrained networks.

4259d5dd68242a07189e406d.title_original: Synthetic Neurosymbolic Task Generation with Controlled Constraint Complexity
4259d5dd68242a07189e406d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19597v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce NeSySy, a synthetic generator for neurosymbolic learning tasks that jointly produces logical constraints and consistent datasets. Unlike existing benchmarks, NeSySy provides fine-grained control over key properties such as constraint structure, tightness, input dependence, and data generation and alignment strategies. In particular, it allows the use of rich constraints over infinite domains, and uses solvers to ensure that the constraints are meaningful and that generated samples satisfy the constraints. We design NeSySy to support both learning with declarative constraints and learning from distant supervision. Across a range of constraint families, we provide evidence that its parameters induce systematic and largely independent effects on task difficulty. Using NeSySy, we study constraint-aware learning methods, identifying regimes where explicit constraint enforcement is beneficial and where expressive unconstrained models can instead learn constraint structure directly from data. Our results establish NeSySy as a controlled testbed for analysing the interaction between learning and logical structure. NeSySy is built around a pipeline that incorporates solvers. Satisfiability checkers (CNFgen and Z3) generate and certify constraints. Constrained optimizers (RC2 for MaxSAT, Z3 for OMT) compute optimal repairs that guarantee every generated sample is consistent.

52ef49f867a77656a97de581.title_original: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
52ef49f867a77656a97de581.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. On the Norwegian North Sea benchmark, GeoLog-Agent achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.9307 and a peak $R^2$ of 0.9713. It exceeds the nine-baseline average $R^2$ of 0.8387 by 0.0920, with a 30.97% average RMSE reduction, and exceeds the strongest baseline by 0.0274--0.0498 in $R^2$, with 16.25%--24.05% lower RMSE. Ablations confirm the effectiveness and synergy of geological prior reasoning, multi-scale dilated generation, and conditional adversarial modules. Transferring the coupling mechanism to six conventional deep learning models improves their $R^2$ by 0.0162--0.0789 with cross-well stability. These results demonstrate how foundation-model domain reasoning can constrain deep generative reconstruction of missing petrophysical measurements.

7f899bc8fff71eedbb5362e4.title_original: Robust Well-Log Reconstruction Across Point Gaps and Whole Wells via Boundary-Gated Soft-Thresholding Kalman Fusion
7f899bc8fff71eedbb5362e4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Missing wireline logs hinder subsurface characterization. Deep reconstruction networks suffer from gap-boundary steps and cross-basin shifts, while interpolation and Gaussian smoothers struggle with long intervals and outliers. We propose boundary-gated soft-thresholding Kalman fusion (ST-KF), unifying multiresolution wavelet shrinkage, distance-gated residual prior learning, and closed-form robust Kalman smoothing with learning--inference decoupling. Across two public benchmarks totaling 263 wells in the Norwegian North Sea and New Zealand's Taranaki Basin, ST-KF ranks first over 0.15--100-m anchored gaps with 0.09% parameter overhead. Against the strongest of nine baselines, pooled RMSE falls by 5.0%--8.3% for bulk density and 6.4%--15.6% for compressional slowness; against the four strongest baselines, reductions are 0.7%--4.1% for neutron porosity and 1.3%--2.9% for photoelectric factor. Ablations and sensitivity analyses confirm operator synergy and stable performance: removing state-space fusion increases short-gap errors by up to 58.8%, while zero-shot transfer cuts anchored errors by 14%--68%. The results show that local borehole continuity transfers across basins whereas cross-property mappings shift with regional geology, supporting measurement-guided log reconstruction.

b9c40b491452170a4bd556fd.title_original: Where slide-level foundation-model classifiers fail on atypical breast lesions
b9c40b491452170a4bd556fd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether a ductal breast lesion is called atypical hyperplasia or low-grade carcinoma in situ increasingly determines surgery. However, slide-level classifiers built on pathology foundation models (PFMs) perform worst on these lesions. Using four PFMs, cross-validation on BRACS and preregistered hypotheses, we studied where the classification of atypia fails. Because slides are labelled with their most severe lesion, only 39% of the slides with annotated atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) were labelled ADH. Attention ranked the lesion high but rarely first, and showing the model only the lesion helped little, whereas classifiers trained per decision with lesion-level labels improved all four atypical boundaries. ADH regions inserted into benign slides raised the probability of malignancy more than that of atypia. In a hospital with pathologist-labelled single-subtype slides and in HISTAI, benign slides were scored closer to lesions and triage specificity fell from 0.48-0.53 to 0.00-0.07 and 0.22.

a13f2a29c545029d2c39030f.title_original: ROUNDS: Source-Framed Diagnostic Revision after Multi-Turn Clinical Evidence
a13f2a29c545029d2c39030f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high scores on medical benchmarks, but does this performance translate into reliable diagnosis as a conversation unfolds? In diagnostic conversations, users can provide clinical findings across multiple turns, ask for a diagnosis without supplying answer options, and introduce opinions from others. Models must therefore form diagnoses from the available evidence and decide how to respond to subsequent advice. We introduce ROUNDS, a framework that evaluates these abilities after a fixed sequence of clinical evidence delivered over multiple turns. ROUNDS compares diagnosis with and without answer options, presents the same incorrect diagnosis under clinician and lay framing, and varies support for competing diagnoses in written five-clinician panels. Across seven models and 1,035 cases from five datasets, average accuracy was 76.9% with answer options and 57.0% without them. Clinician-framed misleading advice produced lower final accuracy than lay-framed advice in every model, with differences of 4.6 to 38.2 percentage points. Initially correct diagnoses more often became incorrect answers than abstentions, and many adopted the suggested disease. Conversely, accuracy increased as more panel members supported the correct diagnosis, including when the majority opinion remained unchanged. a13f2a29c545029d2c39030f.title_ko: ROUNDS 연구, 의료 AI가 다중 대화와 의사 명의의 오진 조언에 취약
a13f2a29c545029d2c39030f.summary_ko: 연구진은 임상 증거를 여러 차례 제공한 뒤 진단과 의견 수용을 평가하는 ROUNDS로 모델 7종과 사례 1,035건을 분석했다. 평균 정확도는 선택지가 있을 때 76.9%, 없을 때 57.0%였으며, 같은 잘못된 진단 조언도 의사의 의견으로 제시하면 일반인의 의견으로 제시할 때보다 모든 모델의 최종 정확도가 낮았다고 보고했다.
